q: 为什么内容型应用里「读扩展」几乎总是先于「写扩展」成为问题？
q_en: Why do content-heavy apps usually hit read scaling before write scaling?
scenario: Instagram 式图片社区日活 1 亿：人均每天发 1 张照片，但每刷一次首页触发 100+ 次读。
scenario_en: An Instagram-style photo app with 100 million daily users: each person posts about once a day, but every feed refresh fires over a hundred reads.
options: 因为写操作天生就比读操作慢，跟流量规模无关
因为数据库默认不支持并发读，请求只能排队等待
因为写产生数据、读消费数据，读流量天然远快于写流量
因为读操作根本没法用索引优化，只能对整张表逐行做全表扫描
why: 打开 Instagram 首页就是 100+ 次读（图片元数据、用户信息、点赞数、评论预览），而你一天可能只发一张照片（一次写）。读消费数据，天然比写多得多。
why_en: Writes create data while reads consume it, so in content-heavy applications read traffic grows far faster than write traffic.
options_en: Writes are inherently slower than reads, regardless of traffic scale.
Databases don't support concurrent reads by default, so requests queue up.
Writes create data while reads consume it, so read traffic grows far faster than write traffic.
Reads can't be optimized with indexes at all, so every read does a full row-by-row table scan.
optionExplanations: 写不天然慢——真正的差距在于每次写只产生一条数据，而首页要把它读很多遍。
并发读能力早已是数据库标配，瓶颈不在这里，而在读写数量级的悬殊。
对，一次发帖对应上百次浏览、点赞、评论展示，读天然被放大。
索引解决的是查询速度，不是读写数量本身的差距，这条选项跑偏了。
optionExplanations_en: Writes aren't inherently slower — the real gap is that one write feeds hundreds of reads.
Concurrent reads have long been a standard DB feature; the bottleneck is the read/write ratio, not this.
Right — one post gets viewed, liked, and shown in feeds far more times than it was written.
Indexing speeds up queries, it doesn't explain why reads outnumber writes in the first place.

q: 这种数量级对扩展重点选择有什么直接影响？
q_en: What does that order of magnitude imply for scaling priorities?
options: 应该优先攻克写路径的扩展
读路径收益远大于写路径，应优先做读扩展
读写应该同等力度、一起扩展
这说明写操作本身有性能缺陷，需要重构
why: 读写比到 100:1 说明大部分流量是读；索引、缓存、副本这类读优化手段的边际收益远超写路径，应该先攻克读扩展。
why_en: A hundred-to-one read-write ratio means most traffic is reads, so read-side techniques like indexing and caching pay off far more than write-path work.
scenario: 面试官提到某内容应用的读写比大约是 100:1——一条帖子发一次却被读一百次。
scenario_en: The interviewer says a content app has about a 100:1 read-write ratio: one post is written once but read a hundred times.
options_en: Prioritize scaling the write path first.
Read-path techniques pay off far more than write-path work, so scale reads first.
Scale reads and writes with equal effort.
This means the write operations themselves are broken.
optionExplanations: 把力气花在写路径上，管不住已经逼近上限的那 100 份读流量。
对，100:1 意味着索引、缓存这些读侧手段收益最大，该先啃这块。
均分力气忽略了读写规模差 100 倍的现实，写侧投入见不到效果。
读写比只是流量结构问题，不能反推写操作本身有 bug。
optionExplanations_en: Spending effort on the write path won't relieve a read load that outweighs it 100 to 1.
Right — at 100:1, read-side techniques pay back the most, so tackle that first.
Splitting effort evenly ignores that reads outnumber writes 100x; write-side work barely moves the needle.
The ratio is a traffic-shape fact, not evidence that the write code itself is broken.

q: 读流量把数据库压垮时，为什么通常「不是能调试解决的软件问题」？
q_en: Why is a database overwhelmed by read traffic usually not just a debuggable software bug?
scenario: 单库扛 5 万读 QPS，CPU 长期 100%、磁盘 I/O 打满，慢查询日志里却没有异常 SQL。
scenario_en: A single database is taking 50k read QPS with CPU pinned at 100% and disk I/O saturated, yet the slow-query log shows nothing unusual.
options: 因为数据库代码是闭源的，所以没法自己修复
因为 SQL 优化器不可控，写代码也没法干预它
因为问题一定出在网络层，跟数据库本身无关
因为撞上了物理极限：CPU/内存/磁盘都有硬上限
why: CPU、内存、磁盘 I/O 都是物理约束，到顶后再聪明的代码也无济于事，只能靠架构手段（索引、副本、缓存）绕开。
why_en: At scale you hit physics: CPU instructions per second, memory capacity, and disk I/O are hard limits that more code cannot overcome.
options_en: It's because database code is closed-source, so you can't patch it yourself.
It's because the SQL optimizer is out of your control, so no code change can steer it.
It's because the problem must be in the network layer, unrelated to the database itself.
It's because you've hit a physical limit: CPU, memory, and disk I/O all have hard ceilings.
optionExplanations: 开源闭源跟性能瓶颈没关系，这是转移话题的干扰项。
优化器可控与否是另一回事，压垮系统的是硬件极限，不是优化器策略。
网络问题会表现为超时或丢包，而不是数据库本身被压垮，方向不对。
对，处理器、内存和磁盘吞吐都有物理天花板；触顶之后代码写得再精妙也没用，得换索引、副本、缓存这类架构手段来绕。
optionExplanations_en: Open- vs closed-source has nothing to do with hitting a performance ceiling — a distraction.
Whether the optimizer is tunable is separate; the real limit is hardware, not planner strategy.
A network problem shows up as timeouts or drops, not a database grinding under load — wrong layer.
Right — CPU cycles, memory, and disk throughput all have physical ceilings; once you hit them no clever code helps, only indexes, replicas, and caches route around it.

q: 把「读扩展」的标准演进路径排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the standard read-scaling progression in the right order.
steps: 水平扩展数据库（读副本 / 分片）
先在单数据库内优化（索引、反范式、硬件）
需求：读多写少，数据库读负载逼近上限
why: 标准演进：先吃掉单库内的免费余量（索引/反范式）→ 再水平扩展（副本）→ 再加缓存层。多数候选人直接跳到分布式缓存，反而丢分。
why_en: Read scaling progresses from optimizing within the database, to scaling horizontally with replicas, to adding external caching layers.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["需求：读负载逼近上限"] --> A["1. 单库内优化
索引 / 反范式"] A --> B["2. 水平扩展
读副本 / 分片"] B --> C["3. 外部缓存
Redis / CDN"]

q: 数据库索引本质上是什么？
q_en: What is a database index at its core?
scenario: 用户表 1 亿行，登录时按 email 做等值查询要毫秒级返回，不能全表扫。
scenario_en: A users table with 100 million rows must answer an exact email lookup in milliseconds, so a full table scan is off the table.
options: 一张有序的查找表，指向数据行
数据的完整副本
一份预先算好并存起来的查询结果缓存
一种数据压缩算法
why: 索引 = 有序查找结构 + 行指针，像书后的索引直接告诉你该看哪几页。没有索引，数据库只能全表扫描逐行找匹配。
why_en: An index is a sorted lookup table pointing to rows, like a book index that tells you exactly which pages to check.
options_en: A sorted lookup structure that points to rows.
A complete copy of the data.
A stored cache of precomputed query results.
A data compression algorithm.
optionExplanations: 对，它是排好序的指针表，让查找不用逐行扫。
如果是完整副本，存储和写开销都会翻倍，索引没那么昂贵。
查询结果缓存记的是答案本身，索引记的是去哪找答案，两者不是一回事。
压缩算法关心的是省空间，不解决"怎么快速定位到某一行"这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right — it's an ordered pointer table so lookups skip row-by-row scanning.
A full copy would double storage and write cost; an index is far cheaper than that.
A result cache stores the answer itself; an index stores where to find it — different things.
Compression saves space, it doesn't solve how to locate a specific row quickly.

q: 无索引全表扫描 vs 有索引查找，复杂度和量级差别是？
q_en: What is the complexity difference between a full table scan and an indexed lookup?
options: O(n) vs O(n)，没有差别
都变成 O(1)
O(n) 降到 O(log n)
O(n²) 降到 O(n)
why: 索引把线性扫描变成对数查找：100 万行的表大约只需 20 次索引比较就能定位，这是读优化里性价比最高的一步。
why_en: An index turns a linear scan into a logarithmic lookup, roughly twenty index checks instead of scanning a million rows.
scenario: users 表有 1000 万行，按 email 精确匹配查询；你要判断加索引后复杂度能改善多少。
scenario_en: The users table has 10 million rows and queries look up users by exact email match; you need to judge how much an index improves complexity.
options_en: O(n) versus O(n), no difference.
Both become O(1).
O(n) drops to O(log n).
O(n squared) drops to O(n).

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种平衡树结构的通用索引，适合范围和排序查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced-tree index structure suited for range queries and sorting.

optionExplanations: 如果真没差别，加索引就没有意义了，但实测差距是数量级的。
O(1) 意味着不管数据多大都一次命中，B-tree 索引做不到这一点，它是对数级。
对，B-tree 把线性扫描压成对数级比较，百万行只需约 20 次。
没有哪种索引能把复杂度往上抬到平方级，这个方向本身就错了。
optionExplanations_en: If there were really no difference, indexing would be pointless — the real gap is an order of magnitude.
O(1) means one lookup regardless of size; a B-tree index doesn't do that, it's logarithmic.
Right — a B-tree turns a linear scan into log-time lookups, about 20 comparisons for a million rows.
No indexing technique makes complexity worse than what you started with — this direction is backwards.

q: 关于索引类型，下列哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about index types are correct? Select all that apply.
scenario: 订单库要同时支持 order_id 精确查、下单时间范围查、商品描述关键词搜三类查询。
scenario_en: An orders database has to serve exact order-id lookups, created-at range queries, and keyword search over product descriptions.
options: B-tree 是最通用、最常见的索引类型
哈希索引适合精确匹配查询
全文搜索、地理查询有各自的专用索引
哈希索引最适合范围查询
why: B-tree 通吃一般查询，哈希只做精确匹配（无序、不支持范围），全文/地理有专用索引。
why_en: B-tree indexes are the general default, hash indexes suit exact matches but not ranges, and full-text or geo queries use specialized indexes.
options_en: B-tree is the most general and common index type.
Hash indexes are good for exact-match lookups.
Full-text search and geo queries have their own specialized indexes.
Hash indexes are best for range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种平衡树结构的通用索引，适合范围和排序查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced-tree index structure suited for range queries and sorting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于哈希表的索引，只支持精确匹配，不支持范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is built on a hash table and supports exact-match lookups but not range queries.

optionExplanations: 对，B-tree 是默认索引，范围查询、排序都能扛。
对，哈希索引专治等值匹配，查找是 O(1) 级别。
对，全文搜索和地理位置各有专用索引结构，不是塞进 B-tree 就能用。
哈希索引没有顺序概念，做不了范围扫描，真正适合范围查询的是 B-tree。
optionExplanations_en: Right — B-tree is the default index, handling ranges and sorting.
Right — hash indexes are built for exact-match lookups, roughly O(1).
Right — full-text and geo queries need their own specialized index structures, not a generic B-tree.
Hash indexes have no ordering, so they can't scan ranges; B-tree is what actually handles range queries.

scenario: 社交应用：用户经常按 hashtag 搜索帖子，商品页常按价格排序；读压力刚开始出现。
scenario_en: In a social app, users often search posts by hashtag and product pages often sort by price; read pressure is just starting to show.
q: 读扩展的第一步该做什么？
q_en: What should be the first read-scaling move?
options: 直接上 Redis 缓存
给高频查询/排序的列加索引
立刻分库分表
换更大的服务器
why: 第一步永远是给频繁查询、排序的列（如 hashtag、价格）加索引——先吃掉单库内的余量，再谈基础设施。
why_en: The first move is indexing the columns you frequently query, join on, or sort by, before adding any infrastructure.
whenOtherWins: 若已有合理索引仍逼近 5-10 万读/秒，才轮到缓存或读副本——索引是第一步而不是全部。
options_en: Add a Redis cache right away.
Add indexes on frequently queried or sorted columns.
Shard the database immediately.
Move to a bigger server.
optionExplanations: 读压力刚冒头就上 Redis，等于在没吃完单库免费余量前就多背一层运维和一致性成本。
对，先给 hashtag、价格这些高频查询列建索引，这是成本最低的第一步。
分库分表运维复杂、迁移风险高，读压力刚起步时用不上这么重的手段。
换服务器能买点时间，但没解决查询本身低效的问题，治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: Reaching for Redis the moment read pressure appears skips the free headroom still sitting in the single database.
Right — indexing hashtag and price columns first is the cheapest move before touching infrastructure.
Sharding brings real operational and migration risk, overkill for read pressure that's just starting to show.
A bigger server buys time but doesn't fix the underlying inefficient query, so it's a stopgap not a fix.

q: 关于「索引太多会拖慢写入」的担忧，面试里的正确姿态是？
q_en: How should you handle the concern that too many indexes slow writes in an interview?
scenario: 读写比 100:1 的电商库要为多个查询模式加索引，面试官追问「不会拖慢写入吗」。
scenario_en: You are adding indexes for several query patterns on an e-commerce database with a 100-to-1 read-to-write ratio, and the interviewer pushes back that writes will suffer.
options: 这种担忧被严重夸大，缺索引比索引过多危险得多
索引确实很危险，加了之后能不加就尽量不加
每张表最多只能建一个索引，多了系统就会报错
索引只影响读取速度，完全不会拖慢任何写入
why: 索引写开销真实存在但通常被夸大，现代硬件能高效处理设计良好的索引。面试里应自信地为查询模式加索引。
why_en: Index overhead is real but overblown, so confidently add indexes for your query patterns because under-indexing kills far more applications.
options_en: This worry is overblown; under-indexing kills far more apps than over-indexing.
Indexes are genuinely dangerous, so avoid adding more than the bare minimum.
Each table can have at most one index, or the system will reject it.
Indexes only affect read speed and never slow down any write at all.
optionExplanations: 对，缺索引拖垮查询的代价远大于索引拖慢写入的代价，该加就加。
把索引当成洪水猛兽会让你在面试里畏手畏脚，反而漏掉明显该加的索引。
一张表只留一个索引会逼你在多种查询模式之间做痛苦取舍，没这个必要。
索引确实会拖慢写入——每次插入/更新都要同步维护索引结构。
optionExplanations_en: Right — under-indexing costs far more than the write overhead indexes add, so add them confidently.
Treating indexes as dangerous makes you hesitant in interviews and causes you to skip indexes you clearly need.
Capping a table at one index forces painful tradeoffs across query patterns for no real reason.
Indexes do slow writes somewhat — every insert or update has to maintain the index structure too.

q: 关于用「硬件升级」应对读压力，最准确的定位是？
q_en: How should you position hardware upgrades for read pressure?
scenario: 面试里读 QPS 已顶到单库物理上限，还剩 20 分钟要交出读扩展方案。
scenario_en: In the interview, read QPS has already hit the physical ceiling of one database and you have twenty minutes left to lay out a read-scaling plan.
options: 硬件升级能解决一切扩展问题，其他手段都不需要
面试官最想听到的答案就是直接加机器解决问题
硬件升级对读扩展毫无帮助，纯粹是浪费预算
无聊但有效：能快速买喘息空间，但不该是面试主答案
why: SSD、加内存、更强 CPU 能快速买时间，但它回避了架构问题；面试里一句带过即可。
why_en: Hardware upgrades are boring but effective for buying headroom, worth mentioning in an interview but rarely what the interviewer wants.
options_en: Hardware upgrades solve every scaling problem, no other technique is needed.
The answer interviewers most want to hear is simply throwing more machines at it.
Hardware upgrades do nothing for read scaling and are just wasted budget.
Boring but effective — buys headroom fast, worth a mention but shouldn't be your main answer.
optionExplanations: 硬件升级买的是喘息时间，架构性的瓶颈（如全表扫描）它解决不了。
面试官想看到的是架构判断力，光靠"加机器"回答会显得没有章法。
更快的 CPU、更多内存确实能立刻缓解压力，说它毫无帮助不准确。
对，硬件升级无聊但真实有效——能买时间，但不该是面试里的主答案。
optionExplanations_en: Hardware upgrades buy breathing room, but they don't fix architectural bottlenecks like a full table scan.
Interviewers want to see architectural judgment; leading with 'just add machines' reads as under-prepared.
Faster CPUs and more memory do relieve pressure immediately — calling it useless isn't accurate.
Right — hardware upgrades are boring but genuinely effective, worth a mention but not your headline answer.

q: SSD 相对机械盘的随机 I/O 提升量级，对扩展决策意味着什么？
q_en: What does SSDs' random-I/O advantage over spinning disks imply for scaling?
options: 提升其实相当有限（1-2倍），不值得当作独立的扩展手段
提升是数量级的（10-100倍），常是最快的第一步
提升虽大但只影响写，不影响读扩展
两者没有区别，应直接上分布式存储
why: SSD 没有机械寻道，随机 I/O 比机械盘快 10-100 倍，是买读扩展喘息空间最快的一步。
why_en: SSDs eliminate mechanical seek time, giving roughly ten to one hundred times faster random I/O, often the fastest way to buy read-scaling headroom.
scenario: 现有系统随机读遇到磁盘瓶颈，你在评估把机械盘换成 SSD 能带来多大的杠杆。
scenario_en: Random reads are bottlenecked on spinning disks, and you are evaluating how much leverage SSDs would add.
options_en: The gain is quite modest (one to two times), not worth treating as a standalone scaling move.
The gain is an order of magnitude (ten to one hundred times), often the fastest first step.
The gain is real but only helps writes, not reads.
There's no real difference; go straight to distributed storage.
optionExplanations: 1-2 倍的提升配不上"没有机械寻道"这个结构性优势，实际差距大得多。
对，去掉机械寻道后随机 I/O 快一到两个数量级，往往是最快能拿到的提升。
SSD 的随机读优势同样直接改善读路径，不是只对写有用。
差距明明存在，跳过 SSD 直接上分布式存储是在放弃唾手可得的收益。
optionExplanations_en: A 1-2x gain undersells the structural advantage of removing seek time — the real gap is much bigger.
Right — eliminating seek time buys one to two orders of magnitude on random I/O, often the fastest win available.
SSDs' random-read advantage directly speeds up the read path too, not just writes.
The gap is real and cheap to capture; skipping straight to distributed storage throws away an easy win.

q: 「范式化 (normalization)」的目的是什么？
q_en: What is the purpose of normalization?
scenario: 电商库里用户名重复存在订单、评论、收藏三张表，存储浪费且改名要多处同步。
scenario_en: In an e-commerce schema the username is duplicated across orders, reviews, and favorites, wasting storage and forcing multi-place updates on rename.
options: 让查询更快
让高并发场景下的写入吞吐更高
把数据拆到多张表以减少冗余
自动生成索引
why: 范式化省存储、避免重复数据，但让查询更复杂：展示一个订单摘要可能要 join 用户、订单、商品多张表。
why_en: Normalization splits data across tables to reduce redundancy, at the cost of needing joins to bring related data back together.
options_en: Make queries faster.
Increase write throughput under high concurrency.
Split data across multiple tables to reduce redundancy.
Automatically generate indexes.
optionExplanations: 把它说成"让查询更快"正好说反了——范式化本身不加速查询，读数据反而常常要跨表拼接。
范式化不直接提升写吞吐，它优化的是存储效率，不是速度。
对，范式化就是把数据拆到多张表、消除重复存储的同一份信息。
索引要单独建，范式化本身不会替你自动生成索引。
optionExplanations_en: Calling it "makes queries faster" has it backwards — normalization itself doesnt speed up reads, it usually forces cross-table joins to reassemble data.
Normalization doesn't directly boost write throughput; it optimizes storage efficiency, not speed.
Right — normalization splits data across tables to stop storing the same fact redundantly.
Indexes have to be created separately; normalization doesn't generate them automatically.

scenario: 电商订单摘要页每秒被读几千次，目前要 join users、orders、order_items、products 四张表才能拼出，系统读远多于写。
scenario_en: An e-commerce order-summary page gets thousands of reads per second and currently joins users, orders, order_items, and products; reads far outnumber writes.
q: 最直接的读优化是？
q_en: What is the most direct read optimization?
options: 建一张冗余的订单摘要单表（反范式化）
给四张表各配一台服务器
把多表join挪到应用层代码里手动执行
每次查询前先开启事务
why: 反范式化把用户名、商品名、价格冗余存进订单摘要表，昂贵的多表 join 变成单表点查——用存储换读速度。
why_en: Denormalization stores redundant copies so an expensive multi-table join becomes a simple single-table query, trading storage for read speed.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["原始读路径"] --> B["users + orders + order_items + products"]
    B --> C["每次页面加载都 join"]
    D["反范式写路径"] --> E[("order_summary")]
    E --> F["页面单表读取"]
whenOtherWins: 若写入频繁、数据总在变，多处更新的复杂度可能不划算——反范式前先看读写比。
options_en: Create a redundant order-summary table (denormalize) so one query returns everything.
Give each of the four tables its own server.
Move the multi-table join into application-layer code and run it manually.
Open a transaction before every query.
tradeoff: 存储与写复杂度 vs 查询速度

termDefinitions.meaning: 故意存储冗余数据以减少查询时的 join，用存储换读取速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately stores redundant data to avoid joins, trading storage for read speed.

optionExplanations: 对，把订单摘要预先拼好存成一张表，读时不用再 join 四张表。
给每张表配服务器只是分散了硬件，四张表还是要各自被查一遍，没有减少 join。
把 join 挪到应用层只是换了个地方做同样的事，网络往返反而更多。
开事务是为了保证一致性，跟消灭多表 join 这件事完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right — precomputing the order summary into one table means reads skip joining four tables.
Giving each table its own server just spreads hardware around; you still query all four and still join.
Moving the join into the application layer just relocates the same work, often adding more round trips.
Opening a transaction is about consistency, not about eliminating the multi-table join.

q: 反范式化之后，用户改名会发生什么？
q_en: What happens after denormalization when a user changes their name?
scenario: 订单摘要页把用户名冗余进 orders 表以省掉 join；用户改名大约一年一次。
scenario_en: The order summary page denormalizes the username into the orders table to skip a join, and users rename maybe once a year.
options: 什么都不用做
必须更新所有冗余副本，写路径变复杂
数据库会自动帮你同步好所有冗余副本
改名操作会被数据库拒绝
why: 冗余数据意味着写时多处更新；好在「改名」远比「看订单」少发生，读多写少时这笔账划算。
why_en: With denormalized data a name change must update every redundant copy, which is acceptable because such writes are rare compared to reads.
options_en: Nothing needs to be done.
Every redundant copy of the name must be updated, complicating the write path.
The database automatically keeps all redundant copies in sync for you.
The rename would be rejected by the database.
optionExplanations: 反范式化后名字被存了多份，什么都不做会留下不一致的旧名字。
对，改名要同步更新订单摘要等所有冗余副本，写路径因此变复杂。
数据库不会替你追踪"这份数据在哪些地方有冗余副本"，同步要应用层自己做。
改名操作本身合法，数据库不会因为存在冗余副本就拒绝它。
optionExplanations_en: After denormalizing, the name is stored in multiple places; doing nothing leaves stale copies behind.
Right — a rename has to update every redundant copy, such as the order-summary table, complicating writes.
The database won't track which redundant copies exist for you; the application has to handle the sync.
The rename itself is a valid write; the database won't reject it just because copies exist elsewhere.

q: 补全反范式化的本质权衡：
q_en: Complete the core denormalization tradeoff.
text: 反范式化用更多{{存储}}和更复杂的{{写入}}，换取更快的{{读取}}；决定之前先看{{读写比}}。
why: 这是「为读优化、牺牲写」的经典例子；写频繁时复杂度可能不值得。
why_en: Denormalization trades extra storage and more complex writes for faster reads, so always check the read-write ratio first.

scenario: 商品页每次加载都要跨 products 和 reviews 两张表计算平均评分，聚合查询昂贵且结果不常变化。
scenario_en: A product page recomputes average ratings across products and reviews on every load; the aggregation is expensive and the result changes slowly.
q: 最合适的手段是？
q_en: What is the best technique here?
options: 每一次页面加载都在线现场重新计算一遍平均分
干脆把评分数据全部删掉，眼不见为净
只是加更多应用服务器来硬扛这份计算量
物化视图：后台预计算并存储，页面直读现成值
why: 物化视图把昂贵聚合「算一次、读多次」，对跨大数据集的分析型查询尤其有效。
why_en: A materialized view precomputes an expensive aggregation once via a background job so every page load just reads the stored result.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[(products)] --> J["后台 refresh"]
    R[(reviews)] --> J
    J --> MV[("product_ratings 物化视图")]
    Page["商品页"] --> MV
whenOtherWins: 若聚合结果必须实时精确反映最新一条评论，预计算的刷新延迟可能不可接受，只能现算或增量更新。
options_en: Recompute the average rating live and on the fly on every single page load.
Just delete all the rating data so there's nothing left to compute.
Just add more application servers to brute-force the same computation.
Materialized view: a background job precomputes the average and pages just read the stored value.
tradeoff: 预计算与新鲜度 vs 实时计算成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 把聚合查询的结果预先计算并存成实体表，读时无需重新计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A materialized view precomputes and stores an aggregation's result so reads skip recomputation.

optionExplanations: 每次现算意味着每次页面加载都要重新 join 和聚合，这正是要解决的昂贵问题。
删掉评分数据是绕过问题而不是解决问题，用户体验直接受损。
加应用服务器只是分摊请求数量，每个请求背后仍然是那次昂贵聚合。
对，后台预算好平均分存起来，页面直接读现成值，不用每次现算。
optionExplanations_en: Recomputing every time means re-joining and re-aggregating on each page load — that's the expensive problem itself.
Deleting the rating data sidesteps the problem instead of solving it, and breaks the feature for users.
More application servers just spread out the request count; each one still runs that expensive aggregation.
Right — a background job precomputes the average and stores it, so pages just read the stored value.

scenario: 要把「商品平均评分」从每次页面加载现算，改成预计算好供直接读取。
scenario_en: You want to replace live calculation of average product ratings on every page load with a precomputed value that pages can read directly.
q: 哪条 SQL 是正确的做法？
q_en: Which SQL statement is the right move?
options: SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id WHERE r.rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY avg_rating DESC;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW product_ratings AS SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.id;
CREATE INDEX idx_reviews_product_rating ON reviews(product_id, rating) WHERE rating IS NOT NULL;
DELETE FROM reviews WHERE rating IS NULL OR rating NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 5 RETURNING id, product_id;
why: 物化视图把 join+GROUP BY 的结果落成实体数据，读时零计算；索引帮不了聚合全表的场景。
why_en: The materialized view stores the join and group-by result so reads skip the computation entirely.
codeSample:
-- 每次页面加载都执行会很贵：
SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id
GROUP BY p.id;

-- 预计算并存储（后台任务定期 REFRESH）：
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW product_ratings AS
SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id
GROUP BY p.id;
whenOtherWins: 数据量小或查询本身便宜时，直接查询即可，不必背上物化视图的刷新维护。
options_en: Query the join and average live on every page load.
Create a materialized view that precomputes the per-product average rating from the join.
Create a partial index on reviews by product and rating, excluding nulls.
Delete review rows with a null or out-of-range rating.
tradeoff: 预计算聚合 vs 每次实时 join+GROUP BY
optionExplanations: 这条 SQL 每次执行都要重新 join 和聚合，正是导致页面变慢的那条查询本身。
对，CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW 把关联聚合的答案提前算好存成表，之后每次读都直接拿现成结果，不必重新跑那次昂贵计算。
索引能加速过滤和排序，但帮不了跨表聚合，这里的瓶颈不是索引能解决的。
删除异常评分是数据清洗，跟"要不要预计算平均分"是两件不相关的事。
optionExplanations_en: This SQL re-runs the join and aggregation every time it executes — it's the very query causing the slowness.
Right — CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW precomputes the joined aggregate and stores it as a table, so every later read just grabs the stored answer instead of recomputing it.
An index speeds up filters and sorts, but it doesn't help a cross-table aggregation — not the bottleneck here.
Deleting bad ratings is data cleanup, unrelated to whether you precompute the average.

q: 这个阈值信号最支持哪个判断？
q_en: What judgment does this threshold signal support?
options: 这个读 QPS 远低于任何需要关注的阈值，完全不用管
已经严重超出经验阈值了，必须立刻分片才行
接近 5-10 万/秒的经验阈值，该扩展或加缓存了
这说明索引本身配置有问题，应该立刻重建索引
why: 5-10 万读/秒是粗略经验值，实际取决于读模式、数据模型和硬件；面试里粗估足以支撑「该扩展了」这个判断。
why_en: As a rule of thumb, a well-indexed single database needs horizontal scaling or a cache beyond roughly fifty to one hundred thousand reads per second.
scenario: 线上监控显示，已经加好索引的单库读 QPS 持续攀升，正朝着经验阈值靠近。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows a well-indexed single database's read QPS keeps climbing toward the rule-of-thumb threshold.
options_en: This read QPS is far below any threshold worth worrying about, nothing to do here.
It's already way over the rule-of-thumb budget, so shard immediately.
Close to the 50,000-100,000 reads/sec rule of thumb — time to scale horizontally or add a cache.
This means the indexes themselves are misconfigured and need rebuilding right away.
optionExplanations: 已加好索引的单库还没到经验阈值前不必担心，但监控显示正在逼近它。
还没真正越过阈值就宣布必须立刻分片，是在没证据时上重手段。
对，逼近 5-10 万/秒的经验阈值意味着该考虑水平扩展或加缓存了。
QPS 攀升是流量增长的信号，不代表索引本身配置有问题。
optionExplanations_en: A well-indexed single database isn't worrying below the rule-of-thumb threshold, but monitoring shows it's approaching it.
Declaring an immediate shard before actually crossing the threshold reaches for a heavy tool without evidence.
Right — approaching the 50k-100k reads/sec rule of thumb means it's time to consider scaling out or adding a cache.
Climbing QPS signals rising traffic, not that the indexes themselves are misconfigured.

q: 读副本 (read replica) 架构中，读和写分别去哪？
q_en: In a read-replica architecture, where do reads and writes go?
scenario: 单主库 MySQL 读 QPS 打满，加了 3 台读副本后要决定读写流量各走哪里。
scenario_en: A single-primary MySQL is maxed on read QPS; you add three read replicas and now must decide where reads and writes go.
options: 所有写都去主库，读可以去任意副本
读写都去主库
写去副本、读去主库
把读和写都随机分配到任意一个节点
why: 副本从主库复制数据；写集中在主库，读分散到副本——这就是读吞吐的水平扩展。
why_en: Read replicas copy data from the primary, all writes go to the primary, and reads spread across the replicas.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    W["写请求"] --> P[(主库 Primary)]
    P -->|复制| R1[(副本 1)]
    P -->|复制| R2[(副本 2)]
    Rd["读请求"] --> R1
    Rd --> R2
options_en: All writes go to the primary; reads can go to any replica.
Both reads and writes go to the primary.
Writes go to replicas, reads go to the primary.
Randomly assign both reads and writes to any one node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主库复制数据的只读数据库副本，用来分摊读流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the database that offloads read traffic from the primary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理所有写入的数据库节点，是数据的权威来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary is the database node that handles all writes and is the source of truth.

optionExplanations: 对，所有写只去主库，读可以打向任意一个副本分摊压力。
如果读写都挤在主库，副本就完全没起到分摊读负载的作用。
这个方向反了——副本是只读的，写永远要回到主库才能被复制出去。
随机分配写请求会让副本各自维护不同的数据版本，直接破坏一致性。
optionExplanations_en: Right — all writes go to the primary, and reads can hit any replica to spread the load.
If both reads and writes crowd the primary, replicas aren't doing any work to offload reads.
This has it backwards — replicas are read-only; writes always go to the primary to be replicated out.
Randomly routing writes would leave replicas holding different data versions, breaking consistency outright.

q: 除了分摊读吞吐，读副本还附赠什么好处？
q_en: Besides spreading read throughput, what extra benefit do read replicas give?
scenario: 已用读副本扛住读量的服务，还要把主库故障的停机时间从小时级压到分钟级。
scenario_en: A service already using read replicas for read volume also needs primary-failure downtime cut from hours to minutes.
options: 还能顺带获得更强的写一致性保证
冗余容灾：故障时可提升副本当新主库
存储成本还能因此变得更便宜一些
还能顺带获得自动分片的能力
why: 副本天然是数据的额外拷贝：主库挂掉时提升一个副本接任，停机时间大幅缩短。
why_en: Beyond spreading read load, replicas add redundancy because a replica can be promoted to primary if the primary fails.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    P[(Primary)] -->|复制| R1[(Replica A)]
    P -->|复制| R2[(Replica B)]
    P -.-> X["Primary down"]
    R1 -->|promote| N[(New Primary)]
    Traffic["读写流量"] --> N
options_en: It also gives you stronger write consistency guarantees.
Failover redundancy: a replica can be promoted to primary if it fails.
It also makes storage noticeably cheaper overall.
It also gives you automatic sharding for free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个副本切换成新的主库，通常发生在主库故障时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Promoting a replica means switching it to become the new primary, typically after the old primary fails.

optionExplanations: 副本能防丢数据，但它同步的是数据副本，不会让写一致性本身变得更强。
对，副本是现成的数据拷贝，主库挂了直接提升一个接任，停机时间大幅缩短。
副本要占用和主库同样规模的存储，谈不上更便宜。
分片是切数据的手段，跟副本要不要能顶替主库是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Replicas protect against data loss, but syncing copies doesn't itself strengthen write consistency.
Right — a replica is a ready-made copy; if the primary dies, promote one and downtime shrinks dramatically.
A replica needs roughly the same storage as the primary, so it isn't actually cheaper.
Sharding is about splitting data; whether a replica can stand in for the primary is a separate question.

q: 补全标准复制架构：
q_en: Complete the standard replication architecture.
text: Leader-Follower 复制：{{主库(Leader)}} 处理写入，多个{{副本(Follower)}} 处理读取；复制可以是{{同步}}的（慢但一致）或{{异步}}的（快但可能读到旧数据）。
why: 这是读扩展的标准复制拓扑；同步 vs 异步的取舍是面试必问点。
why_en: In leader-follower replication the leader handles writes and followers handle reads, with synchronous replication being consistent but slow and asynchronous being fast but possibly stale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制拓扑：一个主节点(leader)处理写，多个从节点(follower)处理读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In leader-follower replication, one primary handles writes while several followers handle reads.

q: 同步复制 vs 异步复制，核心权衡是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between synchronous and asynchronous replication?
scenario: 跨可用区部署的订单库：写入 P99 要 <50ms，又不想让副本读到明显陈旧的数据。
scenario_en: An orders database spanning availability zones needs sub-50ms write P99 while keeping replicas from serving badly stale data.
options: 核心权衡其实是成本高低 vs 占用存储空间大小
两者其实没有实质区别，选哪个都一样
异步复制的一致性反而比同步复制更强
同步一致但写延迟高；异步快但副本可能落后
why: 同步 = 等副本确认才算写完，慢但一致；异步 = 主库写完即返回，快但有陈旧窗口。这是复制延迟问题的根源。
why_en: Synchronous replication guarantees consistency at the cost of write latency, while asynchronous replication is faster but replicas can serve stale data.
options_en: The core tradeoff is really cost versus how much storage space is used.
There's no real difference between them, either one works the same.
Asynchronous replication actually has stronger consistency than synchronous.
Synchronous stays consistent but writes are slower; asynchronous writes fast but replicas can briefly lag.
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 写入延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入要等待副本确认后才算完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Synchronous replication waits for replica acknowledgment before a write completes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库写完立即返回，副本稍后才追上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asynchronous replication returns as soon as the primary commits, and replicas catch up afterward.

optionExplanations: 成本和存储不是这两种复制方式区分的维度，真正的轴是一致性 vs 延迟。
两者的写确认时机完全不同，差别很实质，不是可以忽略的细节。
这个方向反了：异步复制正是因为不等副本确认，才让读到陈旧数据成为可能。
对，同步等副本 ack 才返回、写慢但一致；异步主库提交即返回、写快但副本可能落后。
optionExplanations_en: Cost and storage aren't the axis that separates these two — the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency.
When each mode confirms a write differs fundamentally between them; it's not a detail you can ignore.
This has it backwards — asynchronous replication is exactly what makes stale reads possible, since it skips waiting for acks.
Right — synchronous waits for replica ack, consistent but slower; asynchronous returns after the primary commits, fast but replicas can lag.

q: 复制延迟 (replication lag) 最经典的用户可见症状是？
q_en: What is the classic user-visible symptom of replication lag?
scenario: 用户发完评论立刻刷新，读请求被负载均衡打到落后 200ms 的异步副本上。
scenario_en: A user posts a comment and refreshes right away, and the load balancer sends that read to an async replica running 200ms behind.
options: 写入数据永久丢失
自己刚提交的修改，刷新后看不到
数据库直接崩溃
所有的读请求都会明显变慢、开始卡顿
why: 写进主库后传播到副本需要时间，期间从落后副本读就是旧值。缓解：read-your-writes——该用户的读走主库或粘住已更新的副本。
why_en: With replication lag a user may not see their own change because the read hit a replica that has not caught up, mitigated with read-your-writes routing.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant P as Primary
    participant R as Lagging Replica
    U->>P: update profile
    P-->>U: OK
    U->>R: refresh page
    R-->>U: old profile
    Note over U,R: read-your-writes routes this user to primary
options_en: Written data is permanently lost.
A user can't see their own just-submitted change after refreshing.
The database crashes outright.
Every read request slows down noticeably and starts to stutter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库写入传播到副本需要的时间差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication lag is the delay between a write on the primary and its propagation to replicas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证用户能立刻看到自己刚提交的写入的一致性策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes is a consistency guarantee that a user immediately sees their own just-submitted write.

optionExplanations: 复制延迟只是让副本暂时落后，写入的数据本身仍然安全地在主库上。
对，用户提交的修改还没传播到自己被路由到的副本，刷新看到的就是旧值。
延迟只是数据传播慢，不会让数据库进程本身崩溃。
拖慢的只是读到落后副本的那部分请求，不是所有读请求都会变慢。
optionExplanations_en: Replication lag just leaves a replica temporarily behind; the written data itself is safe on the primary.
Right — the user's own change hasn't reached the replica they were routed to, so a refresh shows the old value.
Lag just means propagation is slow, it doesn't crash the database process itself.
Only requests that land on a lagging replica are affected, not every read request across the board.

q: 读副本和分片 (sharding) 在「数据集大小」上的关键区别是？
q_en: How do read replicas and sharding differ on dataset size?
scenario: 订单表已 5TB，命中索引的查询仍要 2 秒；加了 5 台读副本后延迟毫无改善。
scenario_en: The orders table is five terabytes and even index-hitting queries take two seconds; adding five read replicas changed nothing.
options: 副本复制整份数据，不缩小单机数据集；分片才切开数据
副本反而会缩小单台机器的数据集，而分片其实完全不会
两者其实都能有效缩小每台机器上的数据集
两者都跟单机数据集大小完全没有关系
why: 当数据大到「索引良好的查询也慢」时，副本帮不上忙（每台还是全量数据），要靠分片把数据集切小、同时分摊读负载。
why_en: Replicas copy the full dataset to each server, while sharding splits the data so each database handles a smaller, faster subset.
options_en: Replicas copy full data and don't shrink per-node data; sharding actually splits the data.
Replicas actually shrink each single machine's dataset, while sharding doesn't touch it at all.
Both techniques actually shrink the dataset that lives on each machine.
Neither technique has anything to do with per-node dataset size at all.
tradeoff: 数据集大小分摊 vs 读吞吐分摊

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多个数据库，每个只存一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple databases so each holds only a portion.

optionExplanations: 对，副本是整份数据的拷贝，单机数据量不会变小；分片才真正把数据切开。
这个方向反了——副本复制的是全量数据，不会让任何一台机器的数据集变小。
副本不切数据，只有分片才缩小单机数据量，两者效果并不相同。
分片明明是按数据集大小来切的，说两者都无关跳过了它的核心动机。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a replica copies the whole dataset, so per-node size stays the same; only sharding actually splits it.
This has it backwards — replicas copy the full dataset, so no single machine's data shrinks.
Replicas don't split data at all; only sharding shrinks per-node size, so the two aren't equivalent.
Sharding is literally motivated by dataset size, so calling both unrelated misses its whole point.

q: 「功能分片 (functional sharding)」是按什么来切分数据的？
q_en: What does functional sharding split data by?
scenario: 单库同时装用户资料和商品目录，两类查询互抢 buffer pool，要按业务域拆开。
scenario_en: One database holds both user profiles and the product catalog, and the two query types fight over the same buffer pool.
options: 按每一行数据算出的哈希值来切分
按记录产生的时间范围来切分数据
按业务域切分：用户库、商品库各自独立
按随机数生成的结果均匀分配到各库
why: 功能分片按业务域而不是按记录切分：资料请求只查更小的用户库，商品搜索只打商品库。
why_en: Functional sharding splits data by business domain, putting user data in one database and product data in another so each query hits a smaller database.
options_en: By computing a hash value for each row and splitting on that.
By splitting data according to the time range each record falls into.
By business domain: user data in one database, product data in another.
By a random number generator distributing rows evenly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按业务域切分数据库，比如用户库和商品库分开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Functional sharding splits databases by business domain, such as separating user data from product data.

optionExplanations: 按哈希切分行是常规分片的做法，不是功能分片的定义。
按时间范围切是另一种分片策略，跟"按业务域"这个维度不是一回事。
对，功能分片按业务域切开数据库，比如用户库和商品库各自独立。
随机均分不考虑业务边界，恰恰是功能分片要避免的做法。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting rows by hash is standard sharding, not what defines functional sharding.
Splitting by time range is a different sharding strategy, not the same axis as splitting by business domain.
Right — functional sharding splits by business domain, like keeping user data and product data in separate databases.
Random even distribution ignores business boundaries, which is exactly what functional sharding avoids.

scenario: 全球化产品：美国和欧洲用户各自主要访问本地区的数据，跨洲读取延迟高，单库压力也大。
scenario_en: In a global product, US and European users mostly read data from their own regions; cross-continent reads are slow and the single database is overloaded.
q: 最合适的分片方式是？
q_en: Which sharding strategy fits best?
options: 按用户 ID 算哈希值随机分片，完全不考虑地域
地理分片：数据按区域放本地库，就近读分摊负载
按每张表的大小轮流分片，跟访问地域无关
干脆不分片，只靠加内存硬扛全部流量
why: 地理分片对全球读扩展特别有效：就近服务降低延迟，同时没有任何单库承担全部流量。
why_en: Geographic sharding stores each region's data near its users, cutting latency while spreading load across databases.
whenOtherWins: 若访问没有地域局部性（任何用户随机读全球数据），地理分片收益小，哈希分片分布更均匀；计量单位 ≈ 区域数，不是单条记录数，跨区查询仍是二级成本。
options_en: Hash-shard randomly by user ID, ignoring geography entirely.
Geo-shard: keep each region's data in a local database close to its users.
Rotate shards by table size, regardless of where users are located.
Don't shard at all, just add more memory and absorb all the traffic.
tradeoff: 地理局部性收益 vs 分布不均匀风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理区域切分数据库，让用户读取本地数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geographic sharding splits databases by region so users read from a nearby database.

optionExplanations: 哈希随机分片能均匀分布负载，但完全没利用"用户主要访问本地区数据"这个局部性。
对，把各区域数据放在本地库，用户就近读取，延迟和负载同时改善。
按表大小轮流分片是内部实现细节，跟利用地域访问局部性没有关系。
不分片只加内存治标不治本，跨洲延迟不是内存能解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Hash-random sharding distributes load evenly but ignores the locality that users mostly read their own region's data.
Right — keeping each region's data local lets users read nearby, cutting both latency and load.
Rotating shards by table size is an internal detail unrelated to exploiting regional access locality.
Skipping sharding and just adding memory is a stopgap; cross-continent latency isn't a memory problem.

q: 对「读扩展」而言，分片的正确定位是？
q_en: How should sharding be positioned for read scaling?
scenario: 读 QPS 5 万但数据只有 200GB 的服务要扩读，团队只有 3 个后端工程师维护。
scenario_en: A service at 50k read QPS with only 200GB of data needs to scale reads, and just three backend engineers maintain it.
options: 分片应该是读扩展要考虑的第一个方案
分片几乎不产生任何额外的运维成本
分片和缓存对读扩展的效果完全等价，选哪个都行
分片是写扩展手段、运维复杂；读扩展优先用缓存
why: 分片对读的帮助是「数据集变小 + 负载分摊」，但复杂度高；读扩展优先考虑缓存和副本。
why_en: Sharding is primarily a write-scaling technique with real operational complexity, and for most read problems caching is easier and more effective.
options_en: Sharding should be the very first option you reach for on read scaling.
Sharding barely adds any extra operational cost at all.
Sharding and caching have identical effects on read scaling, pick either.
Sharding is mainly a write-scaling tool with real ops cost; caching is usually easier for reads.
optionExplanations: 分片运维复杂、迁移风险高，读扩展有更简单的第一步可走，它不该是首选。
分片带来跨分片查询、re-sharding 这些真实的运维负担，说它零成本不准确。
分片切数据、缓存存结果，两者解决的问题和代价结构都不同，不能划等号。
对，分片本质上解决的是写扩展和数据量问题，代价是运维复杂；面对纯读压力，缓存和副本通常是更省力的第一选择。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding brings real operational and migration risk; read scaling has simpler first steps, so it shouldn't be the default.
Sharding introduces real overhead like cross-shard queries and re-sharding — calling it free isn't accurate.
Sharding splits data while caching stores results; they solve different problems with different cost profiles.
Right — sharding is fundamentally a write-scaling and dataset-size tool with real ops overhead; for a pure read problem, caching and replicas are usually the easier first move.

q: 缓存对读扩展特别有效，利用的是什么访问规律？
q_en: What access pattern makes caching so effective for read scaling?
scenario: 推特式 feed 里 1% 的热门推文吃掉 90% 的读请求，数据库在重复返回同样的行。
scenario_en: In a Twitter-style feed, one percent of tweets take ninety percent of the reads, so the database keeps returning the same rows.
options: 高度倾斜的访问模式：海量用户反复读同一批热数据
所有 key 其实被完全均匀地访问，没有热点
每份数据都只会被读取一次，从不会重复
这个系统里写请求其实远多于读请求
why: 多数应用的访问高度倾斜——你在反复向数据库要一模一样的数据（爆款推文、热门商品），缓存把这些结果放进内存直接回。
why_en: Most applications have highly skewed access patterns where millions read the same rarely-changing data, which caches exploit by serving it from memory.
options_en: A highly skewed access pattern: millions of users repeatedly read the same hot data.
Every key is accessed with perfectly uniform frequency, no hotspots at all.
Each piece of data only ever gets read exactly once, never again.
In this system writes actually far outnumber reads.
optionExplanations: 对，海量用户反复读同一批热数据，正是缓存能把命中率做高的原因。
如果每个 key 被均匀访问，缓存命中率会很低，收益就没那么明显了。
数据若从不被重复读取，缓存根本存不住任何有用的东西。
写多读少的场景里，缓存对减少数据库压力的贡献本来就有限。
optionExplanations_en: Right — millions of users repeatedly reading the same hot data is exactly what lets a cache achieve high hit rates.
If every key were accessed uniformly, cache hit rates would be low and the payoff much smaller.
If data were never read more than once, a cache would never hold anything worth reusing.
In a write-heavy workload, caching has much less to offer for reducing database load.

q: 缓存命中 vs 优化良好的数据库查询，响应时间量级对比是？
q_en: What is the response-time order of magnitude for a cache hit versus an optimized database query?
options: 都在 100ms 以上
缓存亚毫秒级 vs 数据库几十毫秒
数据库查询通常反而比缓存命中更快一些
两者都在 1 微秒以内
why: 缓存从 RAM 直接返回预计算结果；数据库要读盘 + 执行查询。亚毫秒 vs 几十毫秒是量化「为什么加缓存」的关键数字。
why_en: A cache serves precomputed results from RAM in under a millisecond, versus tens of milliseconds for even a well-optimized database query.
scenario: 设计一个高读流量的资料页，你在决定要不要在数据库前面加一层缓存。
scenario_en: You are designing a high-read profile page and deciding whether to put a cache in front of the database.
options_en: Both are over 100 milliseconds.
Cache hits are sub-millisecond versus tens of milliseconds for the database.
The database query is usually actually faster than a cache hit.
Both are under 1 microsecond.
optionExplanations: 把两者都放到 100ms 以上级别，明显高估了缓存该有的响应速度。
对，缓存直接从内存吐出结果，亚毫秒级；数据库要读盘执行查询，通常是几十毫秒。
这个方向反了——绕过磁盘 I/O 走内存的缓存，天然比数据库查询快得多。
微秒级对多数生产环境的缓存来说也偏乐观，通常是亚毫秒而非微秒。
optionExplanations_en: Placing both above 100 milliseconds badly overstates how slow a cache response should be.
Right — a cache returns straight from memory in sub-millisecond time, while the database has to read disk and run a query, typically tens of milliseconds.
This has it backwards — skipping disk I/O for memory makes the cache inherently faster than a database query.
Microsecond-level is optimistic for most production caches too; sub-millisecond is the realistic range, not microseconds.

q: 应用层缓存（Redis / Memcached）的标准读流程是？
q_en: What is the standard read flow for an application cache such as Redis or Memcached?
scenario: 商品详情页 3 万 QPS：命中要亚毫秒返回，未命中也必须拿到数据库里的最新值。
scenario_en: A product detail page at 30k QPS must return in under a millisecond on a hit and still fetch the current database value on a miss.
options: 永远先查数据库，查完再顺手更新一下缓存
所有读写请求都只经过缓存，数据库彻底被绕开
应用先查缓存，命中直接返回；未命中再查库并回填
缓存会在后台自动跟数据库保持同步，不用应用管
why: 缓存位于应用和数据库之间：命中 = 亚毫秒返回；未命中 = 查库 + 回填。热门数据自然留在缓存里。
why_en: The application checks the cache first, and on a miss queries the database and populates the cache for future requests.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> C{"Cache hit?"}
    C -->|yes| Out["Return value"]
    C -->|no| DB[(Database)]
    DB --> Fill["Set cache"]
    Fill --> Out
options_en: Always query the database first, then update the cache as an afterthought.
Both reads and writes only ever touch the cache, bypassing the database entirely.
The app checks cache first; on a hit it returns directly, on a miss it queries the database and fills the cache.
The cache automatically stays synced with the database in the background, no app logic needed.
optionExplanations: 先查库再更新缓存等于把缓存变成了永远慢一步的旁路，命中率的意义就没了。
只经过缓存意味着数据库彻底被绕开，写入无处落地，这不是缓存的正常用法。
对，先查缓存命中直接返回，未命中再查库并把结果写回缓存供下次用。
缓存不会替你监听数据库变化自动同步，这一步必须由应用主动完成。
optionExplanations_en: Querying the database first and updating the cache after turns the cache into a permanent step behind, defeating the point of hitting it.
Routing everything only through the cache means writes have nowhere durable to land — that's not how caching works.
Right — check the cache first and return on a hit; on a miss, query the database and write the result back for next time.
The cache won't automatically watch the database for changes — the application has to do that sync itself.

q: 在带 TTL 的缓存下，热门与冷门数据会自然形成什么分布？
q_en: With TTL-based caching, how do hot and cold items naturally distribute?
scenario: Redis 只有 64GB 内存，却要挡在 5 亿条商品记录前面，每条缓存设 10 分钟 TTL。
scenario_en: Redis has only 64GB of memory but must sit in front of 500 million product records, each cached with a ten-minute TTL.
options: 热门数据常驻缓存；冷门数据到期自然退出
所有数据永久留在缓存
冷门数据反而常驻，热门数据被优先淘汰出去
缓存内容与访问模式无关
why: 这个模式的妙处：受欢迎的数据（如名人主页）自动留在缓存，不常访问的读到才进缓存、TTL 到期自然回落到数据库。
why_en: Popular data naturally stays cached through constant access while rarely-used data expires after its TTL and falls back to the database.
options_en: Popular data stays cached from constant access; cold data expires after its TTL.
All data stays in the cache permanently.
Cold data actually stays resident while hot data gets evicted first.
Cache contents have nothing to do with access patterns.
optionExplanations: 对，热门数据被不断访问自然续命，冷门数据到期后 TTL 一到就被清出去。
永久保留会让内存被冷数据占满，缓存的自我清理能力就没了意义。
这个方向反了——被频繁访问的数据才更容易续命，冷门数据才是先被清的那批。
TTL 到期的正是那些没人再访问的条目，缓存内容其实紧跟着访问模式走。
optionExplanations_en: Right — popular data keeps getting re-accessed and stays warm, while cold data's TTL runs out and it drops out.
Keeping everything forever would let cold data clog memory, defeating the cache's self-cleaning behavior.
This has it backwards — frequently accessed data is what stays resident; cold data is what gets cleared first.
TTL expiry hits exactly the entries nobody's touching anymore, so cache contents do track access patterns closely.

q: 补全五种常见的缓存失效策略：
q_en: Fill in the five common cache invalidation strategies.
text: 五种失效策略：基于时间的 {{TTL}} 过期；写库时立即更新/删除缓存的 {{write-through}} 失效；把失效事件排队异步处理的 {{write-behind}} 失效；按 {{标签(tag)}} 批量失效相关条目；把 {{版本号}} 编进缓存 key 的版本化失效。
why: 失效是缓存的头号难题；五种策略在「实现复杂度 vs 陈旧窗口 vs 写延迟」上各有取舍。
why_en: The five invalidation strategies are TTL expiry, write-through, write-behind, tagged invalidation, and versioned keys.

scenario: 缓存的是推荐分数这类不太关键、更新模式可预测的数据；实现要尽量简单，能容忍到期前的陈旧。
scenario_en: The cached value is a non-critical recommendation score with predictable updates; the implementation should be simple and stale values before expiry are acceptable.
q: 选哪种失效策略最合适？
q_en: Which invalidation strategy fits best?
options: 分布式锁串行化更新
写时同步失效 (write-through)
只靠 TTL 定时过期
版本化 key
why: TTL 实现最简单，适合更新模式可预测、能容忍到期前陈旧的次要数据——推荐分数正是典型。
why_en: Plain TTL expiration is the simplest strategy and fits non-critical data with predictable update patterns like recommendation scores.
whenOtherWins: 对用户资料、库存这类关键数据，只靠 TTL 的陈旧窗口太大，必须叠加写时主动失效。
options_en: Serialize updates with a distributed lock.
Synchronous write-through invalidation.
Rely solely on TTL expiration.
Versioned cache keys.
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 陈旧容忍度
optionExplanations: 分布式锁是为了防止并发写冲突，对"次要数据、能忍陈旧"这种简单场景是过度设计。
写时同步失效能保证新鲜，但要多改一处代码路径，对推荐分数这种数据不值得。
对，推荐分数更新可预测、能忍到期前陈旧，直接靠 TTL 到期最简单。
版本化 key 要维护版本号和多查一跳，对这种非关键数据是不必要的复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: A distributed lock guards against concurrent write conflicts — overkill for secondary data that can simply tolerate staleness.
Write-through invalidation keeps things fresh but adds a write-path code path — not worth it for a recommendation score.
Right — recommendation scores update predictably and can tolerate staleness before expiry, so plain TTL is simplest.
Versioned keys need version bookkeeping and an extra lookup — unnecessary complexity for non-critical data.

q: 同步失效 vs 异步失效，核心区别是？
q_en: What is the core difference between synchronous and asynchronous invalidation?
scenario: 商品改价场景：写路径延迟预算只有 100ms，要决定失效放在写事务内还是丢给队列。
scenario_en: On a price change the write path has only a 100ms latency budget, and you must decide whether invalidation happens inside the write or goes onto a queue.
options: 前者异步、后者同步
同步失效保一致但拖慢写；异步失效写快但有陈旧窗口
两者都不影响写延迟
write-behind 这种写回策略的一致性反而更强
why: 又是「写延迟 vs 陈旧窗口」的权衡：同步失效保一致但要小心错误处理，异步失效快但有陈旧窗口。
why_en: Synchronous invalidation updates or deletes cache entries during the write path for consistency at the cost of write latency, while asynchronous invalidation queues events and briefly risks stale reads.

rows: 写时立即更新/删除缓存
更大，直到 worker 处理

options_en: The former is asynchronous, the latter synchronous.
Synchronous invalidation updates or deletes cache during the write for consistency but slows writes; asynchronous invalidation queues the event, writing fast but risking a stale window.
Neither affects write latency.
Write-behind, the write-back strategy, actually has stronger consistency.
tradeoff: 写延迟 vs 陈旧窗口
optionExplanations: 这个说法把两者的同步/异步关系直接说反了。
对，同步失效在写路径里立即更新或删除缓存，保一致但拖慢写；异步排队处理，写快但留陈旧窗口。
写路径要不要等失效完成，直接决定写延迟，说两者都不受影响不准确。
write-behind 恰恰是异步排队处理失效，牺牲的正是一致性来换取写速度。
optionExplanations_en: This statement swaps which one is synchronous and which is asynchronous.
Right — synchronous invalidation updates or deletes cache entries inline for consistency but slows writes; asynchronous queues the event, faster but leaving a stale window.
Whether the write path waits for invalidation to finish directly affects write latency — saying neither is affected isn't accurate.
Write-behind is exactly the asynchronous, queued approach, trading consistency for write speed, not gaining it.

scenario: 缓存里有大量与「用户 123 的帖子」相关的条目（列表页、详情页、聚合页），一次帖子改动要让它们全部失效。
scenario_en: The cache has many entries related to user 123's posts, including list pages, detail pages, and aggregate pages; one post update must invalidate all of them.
q: 最合适的失效策略是？
q_en: Which invalidation strategy fits best?
options: 标签失效：按标签一键失效所有关联条目
逐个记住所有 key 再一一删除
把这些条目的 TTL 都设成 1 秒
干脆不缓存这些数据
why: 标签失效专治「一份数据牵连多个缓存条目」的复杂依赖（如给相关条目挂 user:123:posts 标签），代价是要维护标签与条目的关系。
why_en: Tagged invalidation associates entries with tags so one change can invalidate every related entry, at the cost of maintaining tag relationships.
whenOtherWins: 若只是单实体缓存（一条记录一个 key），版本化 key 更简单，不用维护标签关系。
options_en: Tagged invalidation: tag related entries and invalidate them all at once by tag.
Remember every key individually and delete them one by one.
Set all these entries' TTL to one second.
Just stop caching this data.
optionExplanations: 对，给相关条目挂同一个标签，一次失效就能清掉所有关联缓存，不用逐个记 key。
逐个记住并删除每个 key 在条目数量增长后会迅速变得难以维护。
把 TTL 压到 1 秒等于放弃缓存的收益，用极端妥协换取"看起来新鲜"。
不缓存意味着列表页、详情页、聚合页全部退回到每次现查，读压力直接打回数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Right — tag related entries once, and a single tag-based invalidation clears everything linked to it without tracking keys individually.
Manually tracking and deleting every key becomes unmanageable as the number of related entries grows.
Dropping TTL to one second gives up most of the caching benefit, trading it for the illusion of freshness.
Not caching means list pages, detail pages, and aggregate pages all fall back to live queries, dumping load straight onto the database.

q: 「版本化 key (versioned keys)」失效策略的机制是？
q_en: How do versioned cache keys work?
scenario: 用户资料同时缓存在应用层、CDN、浏览器三处，「删除失效」漏删严重，要换思路。
scenario_en: Profile data is cached in the app layer, the CDN, and browsers at once, so delete-based invalidation keeps missing copies and you need another approach.
options: 定期把整个缓存全量清空一遍，简单粗暴
给每一个缓存 key 单独加上一把分布式锁来协调
把同一份数据写两份，互相当作备份
版本号编进 key；更新递增，旧 key 失效
why: 版本化不删除旧缓存，而是换 key 让旧条目变得不可达——简单可靠，但需要跟踪版本号。
why_en: Versioned keys include a version number in the cache key and increment it on update, so old entries become unreachable instead of being deleted.
options_en: Periodically flush the entire cache wholesale, simple and blunt.
Add a separate distributed lock to every single cache key to coordinate access.
Write the same data twice so each copy backs up the other.
Bake a version number into the cache key; bumping it on update leaves the old key unreachable.
optionExplanations: 定期全量清空是个粗暴的兜底手段，跟"给 key 编版本号"这个精确机制不是一回事。
给每个 key 加锁解决的是并发写冲突，跟让旧缓存条目不可达没有关系。
写两份互为备份是容灾手段，不是让旧版本数据自然失效的方式。
对，版本号编进 key，更新时递增，旧 key 因为没人再拼出它而自然失效。
optionExplanations_en: A periodic full flush is a blunt fallback, not the same precise mechanism as tagging keys with a version number.
Adding a lock per key addresses concurrent write conflicts, not making old cache entries unreachable.
Writing two backup copies is a redundancy tactic, not a way to let old versions naturally lapse.
Right — bake a version number into the key and bump it on update, so nobody constructs the old key anymore and it goes stale on its own.

scenario: 生产系统要定失效方案：既有用户资料、库存这类关键数据，也有推荐分数这类次要数据。
scenario_en: You need a production invalidation plan for both critical data like profiles and inventory and secondary data like recommendation scores.
q: 工程上最常见的组合是？
q_en: What combination is most common in production?
options: 全部只靠长 TTL
全部用写时失效、不设任何 TTL
短 TTL 兜底，关键数据主动失效
所有数据都不缓存
why: 多数生产系统组合使用：TTL 兜底保证最终会刷新，主动失效保证关键数据及时更新。
why_en: Production systems combine short TTLs of five to fifteen minutes as a safety net with active invalidation for critical data.
whenOtherWins: 若全部数据的陈旧容忍都宽松且一致，只靠 TTL 是最简单的方案。
options_en: Use only long TTLs everywhere.
Use write-time invalidation everywhere with no TTL at all.
Short TTL as a safety net, with active invalidation layered on top for critical data.
Don't cache any data at all.
tradeoff: 简单统一 vs 按数据分层保护
optionExplanations: 只靠长 TTL 对用户资料、库存这类关键数据的陈旧窗口太大，兜不住实时性要求。
全部写时失效意味着每次写都要触碰缓存层，对次要数据这个成本没必要。
对，短 TTL 兜底保证最终刷新，关键数据再叠加主动失效，两者分层保护。
完全不缓存等于放弃缓存带来的全部收益，用极端方式规避一致性问题。
optionExplanations_en: Relying only on a long TTL leaves too wide a staleness window for critical data like profiles and inventory.
Write-time invalidation everywhere means every write touches the cache layer — unnecessary cost for secondary data.
Right — a short TTL as a safety net covers eventual freshness, with active invalidation layered on for critical data.
Not caching at all throws away every benefit of caching just to sidestep the consistency question.

scenario: 需求文档写明：搜索结果的陈旧不得超过 30 秒，用户资料可容忍 5 分钟陈旧。
scenario_en: The requirements say search results may be stale for at most 30 seconds, while user profiles may be stale for 5 minutes.
q: 缓存 TTL 应该怎么定？
q_en: How should you choose cache TTLs?
options: 由陈旧性需求驱动：搜索 30 秒、资料 5 分钟
统一都设成 1 小时，图个省事从此再也不用多想
全部设成 1 秒，反正越短肯定越好
随便挑一个数字设上，出问题以后再调整
why: 理想的 TTL 由非功能需求的 staleness 上限直接给出：这让一致性保证有界，缓存决策不用拍脑袋。
why_en: Drive TTLs from your staleness requirements, so a thirty-second staleness budget means exactly a thirty-second TTL.
whenOtherWins: 若需求是「写后立即可见」，多短的 TTL 都不够，要改用主动失效或版本化 key。
options_en: Drive it directly from staleness requirements: 30 seconds for search, 5 minutes for profiles.
Set one hour everywhere for simplicity and never think about it again.
Set one second everywhere, since shorter always has to be better.
Pick a number at random and just fix it later if something breaks.
tradeoff: 一致性保证 vs 缓存收益
optionExplanations: 对，30 秒和 5 分钟直接对应各自的陈旧容忍上限，TTL 就该照这个设。
统一 1 小时会让搜索结果的陈旧远超 30 秒的要求，违反了给定约束。
全设 1 秒会让缓存命中率暴跌，等于交了缓存的税却没拿到缓存的好处。
拍脑袋定 TTL 意味着一致性保证是不确定的，出问题时说不清是哪里错了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — 30 seconds and 5 minutes map directly to each item's staleness budget, so set TTLs from that.
A blanket 1-hour TTL would leave search results stale far past the required 30 seconds, violating the given constraint.
Setting everything to one second would tank the hit rate — paying caching's overhead without getting its benefit.
Picking TTLs arbitrarily means the consistency guarantee is undefined, so failures are hard to trace back to a cause.

q: 关于现代 CDN 的能力，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about modern CDNs is correct?
scenario: 全球读者访问的新闻站，想让边缘节点连个性化首页 HTML 也一起扛掉。
scenario_en: A news site with readers worldwide wants edge nodes to absorb even the personalized homepage HTML.
options: 只能缓存静态文件，不支持任何动态数据
必须自建全球边缘机房才能用
缓存内容不能设置过期时间
除静态资源外，也能缓存动态内容
why: CDN 起家于静态资源，但现代 CDN 也缓存动态内容，把缓存从你的机房延伸到全球边缘节点。
why_en: Modern CDNs cache dynamic content such as API responses and query results, not just static assets.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["User"] --> E["Nearest CDN edge"]
    E -->|hit| U
    E -->|miss| O["Origin / API"]
    O --> E
options_en: It can only cache static files and never handles dynamic data.
It requires building your own global edge data centers.
Cached content can never have an expiration set.
Beyond static assets, modern CDNs also cache dynamic content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers located near users.

optionExplanations: 现代 CDN 早已能缓存 API 响应、查询结果这类动态内容，不止静态文件。
主流 CDN 服务本身就提供全球边缘网络，不需要自建机房才能用。
缓存内容设置过期时间（如 Cache-Control）正是 CDN 控制新鲜度的常规手段。
对，现代 CDN 除了静态资源，也能缓存 API 响应等动态内容。
optionExplanations_en: Modern CDNs can already cache dynamic content like API responses and query results, not just static files.
Mainstream CDN providers already run a global edge network for you — no need to build your own data centers.
Setting an expiration via headers like Cache-Control is exactly how CDNs normally control freshness.
Right — beyond static assets, modern CDNs also cache dynamic content such as API responses.

q: 东京用户访问弗吉尼亚源站 vs 就近的东京边缘节点，延迟量级变化是？
q_en: What latency change do you expect from a Virginia origin to a Tokyo edge node?
options: 约 200ms 降到 10ms 以内
没有变化
从 1 秒降到 500ms
延迟反而从 10ms 升到 200ms
why: 地理分布是 CDN 的核心价值：跨洲往返约 200ms，就近边缘 10ms 以内，且命中的请求完全不打源站。
why_en: Edge caching cuts response times from around two hundred milliseconds cross-continent to under ten milliseconds locally.
scenario: 服务部署在美国弗吉尼亚，东京用户抱怨页面慢，你在评估是否要上 CDN 边缘节点。
scenario_en: The service is hosted in Virginia and Tokyo users complain about slow pages; you are evaluating CDN edge nodes.
options_en: From about 200 milliseconds down to under 10 milliseconds.
No change at all.
From 1 second down to 500 milliseconds.
Latency actually rises from 10 milliseconds to 200 milliseconds.
optionExplanations: 对，跨洲往返约 200ms，换到就近的东京边缘节点能压到 10ms 以内，命中的请求完全不打源站。
地理距离直接决定网络往返时间，从弗吉尼亚到东京不可能毫无变化。
1 秒和 500ms 都远高于实际跨洲往返延迟的量级，估得太夸张。
这个方向反了——边缘节点离用户更近，延迟应该是降而不是升。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a cross-continent round trip is roughly 200 milliseconds, and a local Tokyo edge node brings that under 10 milliseconds.
Geographic distance directly drives round-trip time; going from Virginia to Tokyo can't leave latency unchanged.
Both 1 second and 500 milliseconds are far above the real magnitude of a cross-continent round trip — overestimated.
This has it backwards — an edge node is physically closer to the user, so latency should drop, not climb.

q: 读密集应用配好 CDN 缓存后，源站负载大致能降多少？
q_en: Roughly how much can a well-configured CDN reduce origin load in a read-heavy app?
options: 90% 或更多
基本不变
正好一半
why: 商品页、公开资料、搜索结果这类多人共读的内容都能边缘化，命中的请求完全不到源站，降 90%+ 很常见。
why_en: For read-heavy applications CDN caching can offload ninety percent or more of origin traffic.
scenario: 读密集应用给公开内容加上 CDN 边缘缓存后，你要向团队量化能省下多少源站压力。
scenario_en: After adding CDN edge caching for public content in a read-heavy app, you need to quantify the origin-load reduction.
options_en: About 10%.
90% or more.
Essentially unchanged.
Exactly half.
optionExplanations: 10% 低估了共享型公开内容能被边缘化命中的比例，实际收益比这大得多。
对，商品页、公开资料这类多人共读内容命中缓存后完全不打源站，降 90%+ 很常见。
配好 CDN 后源站流量基本不变说明缓存根本没生效，跟题设矛盾。
读密集内容的命中率通常远高于 50%，"正好一半"低估了 CDN 的效果。
optionExplanations_en: 10% understates how much shared, publicly-read content gets offloaded to the edge — the real gain runs much higher.
Right — shared content like product pages and public profiles never touches the origin on a cache hit, so 90%+ reduction is common.
Origin traffic staying essentially unchanged would mean the CDN isn't actually caching anything — contradicts the premise.
Read-heavy content typically sees a hit rate well above 50%; 'exactly half' undersells what a CDN delivers.

scenario: 决定哪些内容进 CDN：候选有公开帖子、商品目录、搜索结果、用户私信、个人偏好设置。
scenario_en: You are deciding what should go into the CDN: public posts, product catalogs, search results, private messages, and personal settings.
q: 正确的取舍是？
q_en: What is the right CDN caching tradeoff?
options: 把所有内容全部塞进 CDN，越多越好
只缓存私信，因为它最敏感
全都不进 CDN
公开内容进 CDN，私有数据不进
why: CDN 只对「多用户共读」的内容有意义；私信、个人设置这类单用户数据只有本人访问，放 CDN 没有命中率收益。
why_en: CDNs only make sense for content many users share, so cache public posts and catalogs but never user-specific data that only one person requests.
whenOtherWins: 单用户数据要提速应放应用层缓存或客户端缓存，而不是共享型的 CDN。
options_en: Put all content into the CDN, the more the better.
Only cache private messages since they're the most sensitive.
Don't use a CDN for anything.
Cache public posts, catalogs, and search results; skip single-user data like DMs and settings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠近用户的 CDN 节点，命中时直接返回内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge server is a CDN node near users that returns cached content directly.

optionExplanations: 把私信、个人设置这些只被一位用户访问的数据也塞进 CDN，命中率极低，白白浪费边缘容量。
私信恰恰是最不该进 CDN 的数据——它只被一个人访问，不存在多用户共读的收益。
完全不用 CDN 等于放弃公开内容能带来的巨大命中率和延迟收益。
对，把帖子、商品目录这类会被很多人重复访问的内容放进 CDN，只有本人会看的数据留在应用层就好。
optionExplanations_en: Stuffing data only one user ever sees, like DMs or settings, into the CDN gets near-zero hit rate — wasted edge capacity.
Private messages are exactly the wrong candidate — only one person reads them, so there's no shared-read benefit.
Skipping the CDN entirely throws away the huge hit-rate and latency win available for public content.
Right — put content many people repeatedly read, like posts and catalogs, in the CDN, and leave anything only one person ever sees at the application layer.

scenario: 面试进入扩展性讨论环节，你的系统是读密集型。
scenario_en: The interview has moved into scalability, and your system is read-heavy.
q: 最加分的切入方式是？
q_en: What is the strongest way to start the scalability discussion?
options: 直接宣布「加 Redis 和 CDN」
主动指出读瓶颈，按查询优化到缓存副本展开
等面试官点名再讨论
先谈微服务拆分
why: 强候选人主动识别读瓶颈：画 API 时就在会被打爆的端点停下来量化问题（如「资料页每天数十亿读」），然后按查询优化 → 缓存/副本的顺序展开。
why_en: Strong candidates proactively flag high-volume endpoints, quantify the read load, and then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
whenOtherWins: 若系统是写密集（如 Uber 位置上报），应先谈写扩展而不是读扩展。
options_en: Just announce 'add Redis and a CDN'.
Proactively call out read bottlenecks at high-traffic endpoints, then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
Wait for the interviewer to bring it up.
Start by talking about microservice decomposition.
optionExplanations: 直接宣布方案却没有先量化瓶颈，会让面试官看不到你判断问题的过程。
对，画到高流量端点时主动停下量化问题，再按查询优化到缓存/副本的顺序展开。
被动等面试官点名会显得你没有主动发现问题的习惯，这是候选人该主动做的事。
系统是读密集型时先讲微服务拆分是跑题，没有先处理眼下真正的瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Announcing a solution without first quantifying the bottleneck leaves the interviewer unable to see your reasoning process.
Right — pause at the high-traffic endpoint to quantify it, then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
Waiting passively for the interviewer to raise it signals you don't proactively spot problems — that's on the candidate to drive.
Leading with microservice decomposition on a read-heavy system is off-topic when the actual bottleneck hasn't been addressed yet.

scenario: 设计 Bitly：一条短链创建一次却可能被点击数百万次，长短链映射一旦生成从不改变。
scenario_en: Designing Bitly: a short link is created once, may be clicked millions of times, and the long-to-short mapping never changes.
q: 缓存策略应该是？
q_en: What caching strategy fits Bitly?
options: 设一个很短的 TTL，让它频繁刷新保持新鲜
干脆不缓存，用不缓存的方式防止数据陈旧
Redis 激进缓存不过期，配 CDN 扛流量
只把热门链接缓存 1 分钟，冷门链接不管
why: 极端读写比 + 不可变数据 = 缓存梦想场景：不设过期也不会陈旧，命中率极高。
why_en: Bitly is a caching dream because the mapping never changes, so cache it aggressively with no expiration and let the CDN absorb global traffic.
whenOtherWins: 只要数据可能变（比如允许修改目标地址），「永不过期」就不成立，必须引入失效机制。
options_en: Set a very short TTL and refresh it frequently to stay fresh.
Don't cache at all, so staleness simply can't happen.
Cache the mapping aggressively in Redis with no expiration, backed by a CDN for global traffic.
Only cache popular links for one minute and leave the rest uncached.
tradeoff: 激进缓存命中率 vs 数据不可变前提
optionExplanations: 设一个很短的 TTL 让它频繁刷新，映射从不改变，白白丢弃缓存收益。
不缓存会让每次点击都直接打数据库，白白浪费了这份数据天生的缓存友好性。
对，映射不可变，Redis 可以激进缓存不设过期，CDN 再兜住全球流量。
只缓存 1 分钟等于人为制造陈旧风险，而这份数据其实从不会陈旧。
optionExplanations_en: Set a very short TTL and refresh it frequently — the mapping never changes, so this just throws away caching benefit.
Not caching sends every click straight to the database, wasting data that's naturally perfect for caching.
Right — the mapping is immutable, so cache it aggressively in Redis with no expiration, backed by a CDN for global traffic.
Capping it at one minute manufactures staleness risk for data that, in reality, never goes stale.

scenario: 设计 Ticketmaster：开票瞬间几千人狂刷同一活动页；页面包含活动详情、场馆信息、座位图，也包含实时座位余量。
scenario_en: Designing Ticketmaster: at sale time thousands of users refresh the same event page; it includes event details, venue info, seat maps, and live seat availability.
q: 正确的缓存边界是？
q_en: Where should the caching boundary be?
options: 稳定内容激进缓存，余量近似，购买查权威库存
把整个页面不分内容全部缓存 10 分钟，图省事
什么都不缓存，靠这个办法保证绝对正确
把座位余量也一起缓存 60 秒，跟其他内容一视同仁
why: 关键是划清「可缓存内容」和「必须强一致的库存路径」：活动详情、场馆、座位图可激进缓存，余量只做短 TTL 近似展示。购买路径必须查权威库存，用锁或事务原子预留。
why_en: Cache stable event details aggressively; seat availability can be approximate for display, but checkout must read authoritative inventory and reserve atomically.
whenOtherWins: 若展示允许近似余量（如「少量余票」标签），可短缓存近似值，但下单扣减路径必须强一致。
options_en: Cache stable content like event and venue details aggressively; keep seat counts approximate, and read authoritative inventory at checkout.
Cache the entire page indiscriminately for 10 minutes, the simple way out.
Cache nothing at all across the board, relying on that alone for correctness.
Cache seat availability too for 60 seconds, treating it just like everything else.
tradeoff: 缓存吞吐 vs 库存强一致性
optionExplanations: 对，活动详情、场馆、座位图激进缓存，余量只做近似展示，购买时查权威库存并原子预留。
整页缓存 10 分钟会让座位余量长时间不准，购买路径也可能读到过期库存。
完全不缓存会让开票瞬间的巨大读压力直接打向数据库，正确性没问题但撑不住流量。
座位余量缓存 60 秒对购买决策仍然太陈旧，超卖风险没有真正被消除。
optionExplanations_en: Right — cache event, venue, and seat-map details aggressively, keep availability approximate, and route checkout through authoritative inventory with an atomic reservation.
Caching the whole page for 10 minutes leaves seat availability stale for a long stretch, and checkout could read outdated inventory too.
Caching nothing keeps correctness but sends the sale-moment read spike straight at the database, which won't hold up.
Even a 60-second cache on seat availability is too stale for a purchase decision — the overselling risk isn't actually gone.

scenario: 设计 Facebook 信息流：读极其密集，用户通常只看头几条。
scenario_en: Designing a Facebook feed: reads are extremely heavy, and users usually only look at the first few items.
q: 读扩展的关键手法是？
q_en: What is the key read-scaling technique?
options: 每一次请求都从头开始全量重新计算一遍完整 feed
把整个 feed 内容一次性全部发给客户端
完全不缓存任何一条帖子，只为保证绝对新鲜
预计算 feed，缓存近期帖子，用分页避免全量加载
why: 关键洞察：用户通常只读头几条，所以激进缓存近期内容回报巨大；预计算 + 分页避免每次现算和全量传输，把资源砸在头部内容上。
why_en: Pre-compute feeds for active users, cache recent posts, and paginate, because users typically only read the first few items.
whenOtherWins: 规模小或 feed 要求绝对实时时，请求时现算更简单，预计算反而是浪费。
options_en: Recompute the whole feed completely from scratch on every single request.
Send the entire feed content to the client all at once in one shot.
Cache absolutely no posts at all, purely to guarantee freshness.
Precompute feeds for active users, cache recent posts, and paginate instead of loading everything at once.
tradeoff: 预计算与缓存成本 vs 实时全量计算
optionExplanations: 每次现算意味着每个请求都要重新拉取和排序全部候选内容，白白浪费"只看头几条"这个规律。
把整个 feed 一次性发给客户端会传输用户根本不会看到的内容，带宽被浪费掉。
不缓存任何帖子会让每次刷新都直接打数据库，读极其密集时这撑不住。
对，预计算 feed、缓存近期帖子、分页加载，把资源集中在用户真正会看的头几条上。
optionExplanations_en: Recomputing from scratch means every request re-pulls and re-ranks the full candidate set, wasting the fact that users only see the top few.
Sending the whole feed in one shot ships content the user will never scroll to, wasting bandwidth.
Caching no posts sends every refresh straight to the database, which can't hold up under this much read volume.
Right — precompute feeds, cache recent posts, and paginate, concentrating resources on the items users actually see.

scenario: 设计 YouTube：每次打开首页都要查推荐视频、频道信息、播放量；标题/描述/缩略图很少变化。
scenario_en: Designing YouTube: each home-page load needs recommended videos, channel info, and view counts; titles, descriptions, and thumbnails rarely change.
q: 合理的读扩展组合是？
q_en: What is a reasonable read-scaling mix?
options: 播放量必须在每一次播放之后都实时精确地重新更新一次
激进缓存元数据；播放量最终一致；缩略图走 CDN
元数据完全不缓存，缩略图直接存放在数据库里
全站统一走强一致路径，禁止任何形式的缓存
why: 元数据很少变 → 激进缓存；播放量不需要精确实时 → 最终一致批量更新；缩略图是静态媒体 → CDN。按数据特性分层处理。
why_en: Cache video metadata aggressively, let view counts be eventually consistent with periodic updates, and serve thumbnails from a CDN.
whenOtherWins: 若计数用于计费等要求精确的场景，就不能用最终一致的缓存计数。
options_en: View counts must be re-updated in real time and exactly after every single play.
Cache metadata aggressively; let view counts be eventually consistent; serve thumbnails via CDN.
Don't cache metadata at all, and store thumbnails directly in the database.
Enforce strong consistency uniformly site-wide and forbid any form of caching.
tradeoff: 缓存新鲜度分层 vs 全站强一致
optionExplanations: 每次播放都精确实时更新播放量，等于为一个不需要精确的数字承担巨大写压力。
对，标题描述这类元数据激进缓存，播放量批量最终一致，缩略图走 CDN，按数据特性分层。
元数据几乎不变却不缓存，等于放弃了最容易拿到的那部分缓存收益。
全站强一致会连很少变的元数据也强制走一致性路径，付出的代价和收益完全不成比例。
optionExplanations_en: Updating view counts precisely on every single play pays a huge write cost for a number that doesn't need to be exact.
Right — cache rarely-changing metadata aggressively, batch view counts as eventually consistent, and serve thumbnails via CDN, layered by data behavior.
Not caching metadata that barely changes gives up the easiest caching win available.
Site-wide strong consistency forces even barely-changing metadata through the same heavy path, a cost wildly out of proportion to the benefit.

q: 哪些场景「不该」把读扩展当作主攻方向？（多选）
q_en: Which scenarios should not make read scaling the main focus? Select all that apply.
scenario: 为几个候选系统各选扩展主线：它们的读写比、用户规模、实时性要求都不一样。
scenario_en: You are picking the scaling focus for several candidate systems that differ in read-write ratio, user count, and real-time requirements.
options: Uber 司机位置追踪：每几秒上报一次位置，读写比只有 2:1 甚至 1:1
面试官限定「为 1000 个用户设计」的小规模系统
Google Docs 这类实时协作系统：每次击键都要立即对他人可见
Bitly 短链接跳转服务
why: 写密集系统先做写扩展；小规模一个索引良好的单库就能扛几千 QPS；实时协作要的是实时更新，缓存反而有害。Bitly 恰恰是读扩展的梦想场景。
why_en: Skip read scaling for write-heavy systems, small-scale designs a single indexed database can handle, and real-time collaboration where caching actively hurts.
options_en: Uber driver location tracking: pings every few seconds, read-write ratio only 2:1 or even 1:1.
An interviewer-specified small system for 1000 users.
Google Docs-style real-time collaboration where every keystroke must be visible immediately.
Bitly-style URL shortener redirects.
tradeoff: 写扩展优先 vs 读扩展优先
optionExplanations: 对，读写比接近 1:1 时写路径才是真正的瓶颈，该先做写扩展而不是读扩展。
对，就 1000 个用户这个体量，普通索引配单库轻松应付，上读扩展纯属杀鸡用牛刀。
对，每次击键都要立即让别人看到，缓存的陈旧窗口正好破坏这个实时性要求。
Bitly 读写比极端悬殊、映射又不可变，恰恰是最该做读扩展的场景，不该排除。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a near 1:1 read-write ratio means the write path is the real bottleneck, so scale writes first.
Right — at a scale of 1000 users, an ordinary index on a single database handles it easily; read-scaling machinery here is overkill.
Right — every keystroke needs to be visible immediately, and a cache's staleness window directly breaks that requirement.
Bitly's read-write ratio is extreme and the mapping never changes — it's the poster child for read scaling, not an exception.

q: 「读扩展」的真正目标是什么？
q_en: What is the real goal of read scaling?
scenario: 数据库读 QPS 打满导致超时，同时产品抱怨端到端延迟 800ms 太高，要分清主攻方向。
scenario_en: The database is timing out under maxed read QPS while product also complains that end-to-end latency sits at 800ms, so you must separate the two problems.
options: 让系统里所有请求的响应速度都变得更快
彻底把数据库从整个系统架构里消灭掉
减少数据库读负载；低延迟是另一类问题
把写入的吞吐量尽可能地提高上去
why: 读扩展解决的是「数据库被读垮」；「延迟不够低」是另一个问题、另一套解法，别混为一谈。
why_en: Read scaling is about reducing database load, and pure latency problems call for different solutions like edge computing.
options_en: Make every single request in the system respond faster.
Eliminate the database from the architecture entirely.
Reduce the read load the database carries; pure latency problems are a different kind of issue.
Push write throughput as high as it can possibly go.
optionExplanations: 让每个请求都更快涉及延迟优化，跟"数据库扛不住读压力"是不同的问题。
彻底消灭数据库不现实，也不是读扩展要解决的目标。
对，读扩展的目标是减少数据库承受的读负载；纯延迟问题要用别的手段解决。
写吞吐是写扩展的目标，跟读扩展要解决的问题方向不同。
optionExplanations_en: Making every request faster is a latency-optimization goal, a different problem from the database buckling under read load.
Eliminating the database entirely isn't realistic, and it isn't what read scaling is trying to achieve.
Right — read scaling's goal is reducing the read load the database carries; pure latency problems need different tools.
Write throughput is what write scaling targets, a different problem from what read scaling addresses.

q: 1000 万用户后「按 email 登录」的查询拖到 30 秒、DB CPU 100%，最可能的原因是？
q_en: At 10 million users, email login takes 30 seconds and DB CPU is 100%; what is the likely cause?
scenario: 电商站用户从 10 万涨到 1000 万，users 表只有主键，登录按 email 列查询。
scenario_en: An e-commerce site grew from 100k to 10 million users; the users table has only a primary key and login queries by the email column.
options: 是网络出现了故障，跟数据库本身无关
缺索引导致每次登录都全表扫描千万行数据
是内存条损坏了，硬件本身出了问题
是 SQL 语句本身写错了语法
why: 无索引 = 每个查询全表扫盘；join 会再乘一层（先扫 users 再扫 orders，数十亿次行比较）。解法很直接：给频繁查询的列加索引。
why_en: Without an index every login scans all ten million rows, about two gigabytes of data per lookup, multiplied by concurrent logins.
options_en: It's a network outage, unrelated to the database itself.
Missing an index forces a full table scan on every login across all ten million rows.
It's faulty RAM, a hardware problem underneath everything.
It's a plain SQL syntax error in the query itself.
optionExplanations: 网络故障通常表现为连接失败或超时，不会让 CPU 打满、查询变慢这样持续拖着。
对，没有索引意味着每次登录都要扫过一千万行找匹配的 email，CPU 被拖满。
硬件损坏会表现为随机崩溃或数据错误，不会稳定地拖成"越查越慢"这种模式。
语法错误会直接报错让查询失败，不会是"查询能跑但慢到 30 秒"这种表现。
optionExplanations_en: A network outage usually shows up as failed connections or timeouts, not a sustained CPU-pegged slow query.
Right — no index means every login scans all ten million rows looking for a matching email, pegging the CPU.
Faulty hardware tends to cause random crashes or data corruption, not a consistent 'gets slower under load' pattern.
A syntax error would fail the query outright, not let it run — just slowly, taking 30 seconds.

scenario: users 表 1000 万行，按 email 查询走的是全表扫描 (Seq Scan)，登录高峰时数据库 CPU 打满。
scenario_en: The users table has 10 million rows; email lookups are doing a full table scan, and login spikes max out database CPU.
q: 正确的修复是？
q_en: What is the right fix?
options: CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
VACUUM FULL users;
SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 1;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email_backup TEXT;
why: 在 email 列上建索引，把千万行扫描变成几次索引查找；EXPLAIN 里 Seq Scan 变成 Index Scan、成本骤降就是证据。
why_en: Creating an index on the email column turns the full table scan into a few index lookups, visible in EXPLAIN as the plan switches to an index scan.
whenOtherWins: 若查询是 status + created_at 的组合过滤，需要对应的复合索引，单列 email 索引帮不上。
options_en: Create an index on the email column.
Run a full vacuum on the users table.
Select one row with a limit clause.
Add a new email_backup text column.
tradeoff: 查询延迟 vs 索引维护成本
optionExplanations: 对，给 email 列建一个索引，查询计划就能从全表扫描切换成走索引定位，代价从千万行降到几次比较。
VACUUM 清理的是死元组、回收空间，跟"按 email 查找慢"这个问题不是一回事。
只查一行验证不了整表扫描的问题，也不会让后续的正常查询变快。
加一列跟"按 email 查找要扫全表"没有任何关系，解决不了瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Right — indexing the email column lets the query planner switch from a full scan to an index lookup, cutting the cost from ten million rows to a few comparisons.
VACUUM reclaims dead tuples and space; it doesn't address why lookups by email are slow.
Selecting just one row doesn't verify or fix the full-table-scan problem for normal queries.
Adding a new column has nothing to do with why an email lookup scans the whole table — it won't fix the bottleneck.

q: 复合索引 (status, created_at) 能加速哪些查询？
q_en: Which queries can a compound index on status and created_at speed up?
scenario: 订单表建了复合索引 (status, created_at)，后台要跑「待处理订单按时间排序」等查询。
scenario_en: The orders table has a compound index on status and created_at, and the admin console runs queries like pending orders sorted by time.
options: 只加速单独按 created_at 过滤或排序的查询，跟 status 无关，因为它不在索引最左侧
只要用到 status 或 created_at 任意一列的查询都能被这个复合索引加速
只加速直接用 id 主键做等值匹配的点查，其它列都用不上
能加速 status 及联合 status+created_at 过滤，仅 created_at 不行
why: 复合索引按列顺序（最左前缀）生效：先按 status 排、再按 created_at 排，所以跳过 status 就用不上。列顺序很重要。
why_en: Column order matters in a compound index: an index on status and created_at helps status filters and combined filters, but not created_at alone.
options_en: It only speeds up queries filtering or sorting by created_at alone, unrelated to status, since it's not the leftmost column.
Any query touching status or created_at, in any combination, gets accelerated by this compound index.
It only speeds up point lookups on the id primary key, not other columns.
It speeds up status filters and combined status-plus-created_at filters; created_at alone gets no benefit.
optionExplanations: 复合索引没有最左列 status 时用不上，单独按 created_at 查询同样帮不上忙。
跳过最左列 status、只用 created_at 过滤时，这个复合索引根本用不上。
复合索引不是只服务主键点查，status 和联合过滤都能吃到它的加速。
对，最左前缀规则下它能加速 status 单独过滤和 status+created_at 联合过滤，但跳过 status 单查 created_at 用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Without the leftmost column status present, the index can't be used — filtering by created_at alone doesn't help either.
Skipping the leftmost column status and filtering only by created_at means this compound index can't be used at all.
A compound index isn't limited to primary-key point lookups — status filters and combined filters both benefit from it.
Right — under the leftmost-prefix rule it speeds up status filters and status-plus-created_at filters, but not created_at alone.

q: 名人发帖后，单个缓存 key 从 5 万 QPS 冲到 50 万 QPS 并开始超时——这是什么问题？
q_en: A celebrity post pushes one cache key from 50k to 500k QPS and timeouts; what problem is this?
scenario: 单个 Redis 节点缓存推文详情，某明星发帖后这一个 key 的读流量涨了 10 倍。
scenario_en: A single Redis node caches tweet details, and one celebrity post makes that one key's read traffic jump tenfold.
options: 热 key 打满单个缓存节点
缓存穿透
复制延迟
底层磁盘 I/O 读写达到瓶颈
why: 数据在内存不代表无限吞吐：把同一份数据序列化并通过网络发送 50 万次/秒，单台服务器就是扛不住。
why_en: This is the hot-key problem: one key gets all the traffic and overwhelms a single cache server's CPU and network even though the data is in memory.
options_en: The hot-key problem: one key's flood overwhelms a single node.
Cache penetration.
Replication lag.
The underlying disk I/O reaches its read-write bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问、可能压垮单个节点的缓存 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a cache key receiving unusually high traffic that can overwhelm a single node.

optionExplanations: 对，同一个 key 被打到 50 万 QPS，单台缓存节点的 CPU 和网络先扛不住了。
缓存穿透指的是查不存在的数据绕过缓存直击数据库，跟单 key 被打爆是不同的现象。
复制延迟发生在数据同步阶段，跟单个热点 key 的瞬时流量洪峰不是同一件事。
数据在内存里，瓶颈根本不在磁盘 I/O，是网络和 CPU 先撑不住了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the same key gets hit at 500k QPS, and a single cache node's CPU and network give out first.
Cache penetration is when lookups for nonexistent data bypass the cache and hit the database — a different failure mode.
Replication lag happens during data sync; it's unrelated to a sudden traffic spike on one hot key.
