The data is in memory, so disk I/O was never the bottleneck — network and CPU give out first.

q: 请求合并 (request coalescing) 能把「百万用户同时要同一个 key」的后端压力降到多少？
q_en: How far can request coalescing reduce backend load when a million users ask for the same key?
scenario: 100 台应用服务器共用一个热点 key，缓存刚过期时百万用户同时来要同一条数据。
scenario_en: A hot key is shared by 100 app servers, and the moment it expires a million users ask for the same record at once.
options: 降到零请求，从此完全不再去查后端
恰好 N 个请求，N 是服务器数
降到大约一半
不变，仍是百万级
why: 合并把「无上限的相同请求」压缩成「每台应用服务器一个」：百万用户等同一个结果，后端只看到 N 次查询。
why_en: Request coalescing reduces backend load from potentially unlimited to exactly one request per application server doing the coalescing.
diagram:
flowchart LR U1["用户 x 100 万"] --> A1["应用服务器 1
合并为 1 个在途请求"] U1 --> A2["应用服务器 2
合并为 1 个在途请求"] A1 --> B[(后端 / 缓存)] A2 --> B B -.->|共 N 个请求| B
options_en: It drops to zero requests, never touching the backend again.
Exactly N requests, where N is the number of servers.
It drops to roughly half.
It stays unchanged at the million level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一 key 的多个并发请求合并成一次后端调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request coalescing merges multiple concurrent requests for the same key into a single backend call.

optionExplanations: 彻底不查后端会导致数据永远拿不到最新结果，合并的目标不是完全跳过后端。
对，每台应用服务器最多让一个请求真正穿透到后端，其余的都在等同一个结果。
降到一半仍然是随用户量线性增长，没有把重复请求真正压缩掉。
如果流量完全不变，说明合并根本没生效，这不是它该有的效果。
optionExplanations_en: Never querying the backend at all means you'd never get a fresh result — that's not what coalescing is for.
Right — at most one request per application server actually reaches the backend; the rest just wait on that same result.
Dropping to half still scales linearly with user count — the duplicate requests haven't actually been collapsed.
If traffic stayed completely unchanged, coalescing clearly isn't working — that's not the intended effect.

q: 这段请求合并代码里，inflight 字典的作用是？
q_en: What role does the inflight map play in this request-coalescing code?
options: 把最终结果缓存下来，供之后所有请求长期反复地使用
限制全局并发数
记录哪个 key 在途，后来者共享 Future
统计每个 key 的 QPS
why: inflight 是 key → Future 的映射：第一个请求负责真正取数，后续同 key 请求共享那个 Future 的结果，取完即删。
why_en: The inflight map tracks keys already being fetched so concurrent requests await the same future instead of issuing duplicate backend calls.
codeSample:
class CoalescingCache:
    def __init__(self):
        self.inflight = {}  # key -> Future

    async def get(self, key):
        if key in self.inflight:          # 已有请求在取
            return await self.inflight[key]
        future = asyncio.Future()
        self.inflight[key] = future
        try:
            value = await fetch_from_backend(key)
            future.set_result(value)
            return value
        finally:
            del self.inflight[key]
scenario: 你在实现请求合并 (request coalescing) 来抵御热点 key 的并发洪峰，下面是核心 Python 代码。
scenario_en: You are implementing request coalescing to handle a concurrent flood on a hot key; this is the core Python code.
options_en: Cache the final result long-term so all future requests reuse it repeatedly.
Limit the global concurrency count.
Track which keys already have a request in flight so later callers await the same future.
Count QPS per key.
optionExplanations: 取完立刻在 finally 里删掉了 key，它不是长期缓存，只在请求进行中才存在。
字典里没有任何并发数计数逻辑，它记录的是"哪个 key 在途"，不是限流器。
对，key 存在于 inflight 时说明已有请求在取，后来者直接 await 同一个 Future，不重复打后端。
代码里没有任何计数或统计逻辑，inflight 只负责标记在途状态，不是 QPS 统计器。
optionExplanations_en: The key is deleted in the finally block right after fetching — it's not a long-lived cache, only present while in flight.
There's no concurrency-counting logic in the dict — it tracks which keys are in flight, not a rate limiter.
Right — a key present in inflight means a fetch is already underway, so later callers just await that same future instead of hitting the backend again.
There's no counting or stats logic here at all; inflight only marks in-flight state, it isn't a QPS tracker.

scenario: 已做请求合并，但单 key 仍有 50 万 QPS 持续流量，超出单台缓存节点约 5 万 QPS 的能力。
scenario_en: Request coalescing is already in place, but one key still has sustained 500k QPS, above a single cache node's roughly 50k QPS capacity.
q: 下一步该怎么办？
q_en: What should you do next?
options: 把这个热 key 的 TTL 设得更长一些
咬牙换一台更贵、性能更强的缓存机器
干脆关闭缓存，让请求直接连数据库
缓存 key 扇出：复制多份分摊到多节点
why: 合并解决「重复请求」，扇出解决「单 key 持续洪峰」：把一个热 key 拆成多份副本分摊到多台节点。
why_en: Cache key fanout stores identical copies under multiple keys so clients randomly pick one, spreading the hot key's load across servers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Clients"] --> Pick["random shard key"]
    Pick --> K1["feed:taylor:1"]
    Pick --> K2["feed:taylor:2"]
    Pick --> K10["feed:taylor:10"]
    K1 --> N1["Cache node A"]
    K2 --> N2["Cache node B"]
    K10 --> N3["Cache node C"]
whenOtherWins: 若洪峰只出现在过期重建的瞬间而非持续流量，请求合并或提前刷新就够了，不必付扇出的内存与失效成本。
options_en: Just extend this hot key's TTL a bit longer.
Grit your teeth and move to a pricier, more powerful cache machine.
Just turn off the cache and let requests hit the database directly.
Cache key fanout: store copies under several keys and let clients randomly pick one to spread the load.
tradeoff: 多副本分摊负载 vs 内存与失效成本

termDefinitions.term: 缓存 key 扇出 / cache key fanout
termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一数据复制到多个 key 上分散热点流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache key fanout duplicates data under multiple keys to spread hot-key traffic.

optionExplanations: TTL 延长解决的是刷新频率，不改变单个 key 承受的持续 QPS 总量。
换更贵的机器只是把单点瓶颈的上限抬高一点，持续洪峰迟早会再次打满它。
关掉缓存直连数据库会让数据库直接承受这 50 万 QPS，情况只会更糟。
对，把这份数据复制成多个 key 分散到不同缓存节点，客户端随机挑一个，单点压力被摊开。
optionExplanations_en: Extending the TTL affects refresh frequency; it doesn't change the sustained QPS one key has to absorb.
A pricier machine only raises the single-node ceiling slightly — sustained flood traffic will saturate it again eventually.
Turning off the cache sends that same 500k QPS straight at the database instead, making things worse, not better.
Right — duplicate the data under several keys spread across cache nodes, and let clients pick one at random to spread the load.

q: 缓存 key 扇出（一份数据存十个 key）的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of cache key fanout?
scenario: 为分摊热 key，把一条推文复制成 10 个缓存 key 分散到不同节点，而 Redis 内存有限。
scenario_en: To spread a hot key you copy one tweet into ten cache keys across nodes, but Redis memory is limited.
options: 读请求的延迟会因此大幅上升
缓存命中率会因此必然下降
内存占用成倍增加，失效要清掉所有副本
所有的写入操作都会因此被直接阻塞卡住
why: 扇出用冗余换可用性：多份拷贝多占内存、失效要全清；但在热 key 威胁可用性时，这点冗余是保命的小代价。
why_en: Fanout costs extra memory for duplicate copies and makes invalidation harder since every copy must be cleared, a small price for staying online.
options_en: Read latency rises sharply as a result.
Hit rate is bound to drop because of this.
Memory usage multiplies since data is duplicated, and invalidation must clear every copy.
All write operations end up getting directly blocked as a result.
optionExplanations: 扇出后单次读仍然只打一个副本，读延迟本身不会因此变慢。
命中率不会因为多存了几份同样数据而下降，读的仍然是同一份内容。
对，十份拷贝占十倍内存，数据一变还要把所有副本都清掉，这是扇出真正的代价。
扇出只影响读路径的分布，跟写入是否被阻塞没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: After fanout, a single read still hits just one copy — read latency itself doesn't get worse from this.
Hit rate doesn't drop just because the same data is stored under more keys — clients still find the same content.
Right — ten copies means ten times the memory, and any update has to clear every one of them — that's the real cost.
Fanout only changes how reads are distributed; it has nothing to do with whether writes get blocked.

q: 缓存击穿/惊群 (cache stampede) 的根本触发机制是？
q_en: What triggers a cache stampede?
scenario: 热门商品页 TTL 5 分钟、重建要 10 表 join，峰值有 10 万并发读同一条目。
scenario_en: A hot product page has a five-minute TTL, rebuilding it needs a ten-table join, and peak traffic is 100k concurrent reads of that one entry.
options: 过期是二元的：一瞬间全部涌向数据库
是数据库本身处理速度太慢导致的
是 TTL 设置得太长了导致的问题
是缓存容量本身不够大导致的
why: 越热门的条目雪崩越大、重建越贵（10 表 join、外部 API）伤害越大——等于自己对自己发起 DDOS，10 万并发同一瞬间涌向数据库。
why_en: Cache expiration is binary, so the instant a hot entry expires every concurrent request misses at once and floods the database like a self-inflicted DDoS.
options_en: Cache expiry is binary — one moment it's there, the next it's gone, so every concurrent request misses at once.
It's caused by the database itself being too slow.
It's caused by the TTL being set too long.
It's caused by the cache simply not having enough capacity.

termDefinitions.term: 缓存击穿 / 惊群 / cache stampede
termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存过期瞬间大量并发请求同时未命中、一起打向数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede happens when many concurrent requests miss at the exact instant a cache entry expires.

optionExplanations: 对，缓存条目要么在要么不在，没有中间状态，过期那一刻所有并发请求同时未命中。
数据库慢会让重建变慢、加重击穿的后果，但它不是击穿这个现象本身的触发原因。
TTL 长短决定多久发生一次击穿，不是击穿这个机制存在的根本原因。
容量不足会导致条目被提前驱逐，但击穿的根源是过期这个二元事件本身。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a cache entry is either present or gone with no in-between, so the instant it lapses every concurrent request misses at once.
A slow database makes the rebuild take longer and worsens the fallout, but it isn't what triggers the stampede itself.
TTL length affects how often a stampede happens, not why the mechanism exists in the first place.
Insufficient capacity causes early eviction, but the root cause of a stampede is the binary nature of expiry itself.

q: 用分布式锁防击穿（只许第一个请求重建，其他人等待）的主要缺点是？
q_en: What is the main downside of using a distributed lock to stop a stampede?
scenario: 用 Redis 锁让第一个请求重建热点缓存、其余等待，而这次重建的 P99 要 2 秒。
scenario_en: A Redis lock lets only the first request rebuild a hot cache entry while the rest wait, but that rebuild has a two-second P99.
options: 数据库的负载会因此完全不下降，等于白忙一场
缓存会因此永远无法再被更新
锁本身会占用掉太多的内存空间
若重建失败或太慢，成千上万等待者一起超时
why: 锁保护了后端，但把风险转嫁给等待者：重建一慢，全体请求挂起超时，需要复杂的超时与兜底逻辑，高负载下很脆弱。
why_en: With a distributed lock a slow or failed rebuild leaves thousands of waiting requests to time out, making the approach fragile under load.
options_en: Database load doesn't drop at all despite all this, so it's wasted effort.
The cache can never be updated again after this.
The lock itself ends up using far too much memory.
If the rebuild fails or is slow, thousands of waiters time out together, requiring fragile fallback logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨进程/服务器协调的锁，只让一个请求执行重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across processes so only one request performs the rebuild.

optionExplanations: 锁本身就是为了把并发重建收窄成一个，数据库负载确实降下来了，问题出在别处。
锁只是限制谁能重建，缓存条目仍然会被那一个成功的请求正常更新。
锁的内存开销通常很小，真正的风险不在这里。
对，如果那一个重建者失败或太慢，成千上万等待的请求会一起超时，还得设计复杂的兜底逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: The lock is exactly meant to narrow concurrent rebuilds down to one, so database load does drop — the problem lies elsewhere.
The lock only restricts who can rebuild; the cache entry still gets updated normally by that one successful request.
A lock's memory footprint is usually tiny — that's not where the real risk sits.
Right — if that one rebuilder fails or is slow, thousands of waiting requests time out together, requiring fragile fallback logic.

scenario: 首页缓存 10 万 QPS、1 小时 TTL；你想避免到点集体未命中，又不想引入锁的脆弱性。
scenario_en: A homepage cache gets 100k QPS with a one-hour TTL; you want to avoid a synchronized miss without the fragility of locks.
q: 更聪明的做法是？
q_en: What is the smarter approach?
options: 干脆直接把 TTL 一路缩短到只有短短 10 分钟
概率化提前刷新：越接近过期触发概率越高，重建摊开
过期以后就放任所有请求直接打向数据库
每一次读取都强制重新刷新一遍数据
why: 概率化提前刷新把「同一瞬间的 10 万次重建」摊成「十几分钟里的零星刷新」，多数用户仍拿缓存、少数触发后台刷新。
why_en: Probabilistic early refresh gives each request a growing chance to refresh the entry as expiry nears, spreading rebuilds over minutes instead of one instant.
whenOtherWins: 对绝不容许击穿的最关键数据，用后台定时刷新彻底不让用户触发重建。
options_en: Just shorten the TTL all the way down to only 10 minutes.
Probabilistic early refresh: the closer an entry is to expiry, the higher the chance each request triggers a background refresh.
After it lapses, just let every request hit the database directly.
Force a full refresh on every single read, no exceptions.
tradeoff: 确定性防击穿 vs 分散刷新概率

termDefinitions.term: 概率化提前刷新 / probabilistic early refresh
termDefinitions.meaning: 越接近过期，请求触发后台刷新的概率越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Probabilistic early refresh gives requests a growing chance to trigger a background refresh as an entry nears expiry.

optionExplanations: 缩短 TTL 只是让集体未命中发生得更频繁，没有解决"同一瞬间全部未命中"这件事。
对，越接近过期触发刷新的概率越高，把重建从一瞬间摊开到几分钟里零星发生。
过期后放任所有请求直接打库，正是要避免的那个"同一瞬间全部涌向数据库"场景。
每次读都强制刷新等于放弃了缓存本身的意义，读多快数据库就被打多快。
optionExplanations_en: Shortening the TTL just makes the synchronized miss happen more often — it doesn't stop everyone missing at the same instant.
Right — the closer to expiry, the higher the chance a request triggers a refresh, spreading rebuilds over minutes instead of one instant.
Letting every request hit the database right after it lapses is exactly the synchronized-flood scenario you're trying to avoid.
Forcing a refresh on every single read defeats caching's whole purpose — the database gets hit as fast as reads come in.

scenario: 最关键的首页缓存：不能冒任何击穿风险，也不接受概率化方案的不确定性。
scenario_en: This is the most critical homepage cache: no stampede risk is acceptable, and probabilistic behavior is not acceptable.
q: 该用什么方案？
q_en: Which approach should you use?
options: 后台持续提前刷新，用户永不触发重建
干脆把这个条目的 TTL 设得再长一些
用分布式锁来控制谁能重建这个条目
干脆放弃缓存这个条目，每次都现查
why: 后台持续刷新是最强保险：用户请求永远命中新鲜缓存。代价是基础设施复杂度和「刷新了没人读的数据」的浪费，只留给最关键内容。
why_en: A background process continuously refreshes critical entries before expiry so users never trigger rebuilds, at the cost of extra infrastructure and wasted refreshes.
whenOtherWins: 普通热度的数据用概率化提前刷新就够了，专职后台刷新的成本不值得。
options_en: A background process keeps refreshing entries before they lapse, so users never trigger a rebuild.
Just set this entry's TTL to something even longer.
Use a distributed lock to control who gets to rebuild it.
Just stop caching this entry and query live every time.
optionExplanations: 对，后台在过期前持续刷新，用户请求永远命中新鲜缓存，代价是额外的基础设施和一些浪费的刷新。
更长的 TTL 只是把集体未命中推迟发生，风险本身并没有被消除，跟"绝不冒风险"的要求不符。
分布式锁仍然把风险转嫁给等待者——重建一慢，等待者集体超时，跟"不接受不确定性"的要求相悖。
放弃缓存这个条目意味着每次读都直接打数据库，对最关键的首页数据这代价太大。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a background process keeps refreshing before expiry so requests always hit a fresh entry, at the cost of extra infrastructure and some wasted refreshes.
A longer TTL just postpones the synchronized miss — the risk itself isn't removed, at odds with a 'zero risk accepted' requirement.
A distributed lock still shifts risk onto waiters — a slow rebuild still times them out together, at odds with 'no uncertainty accepted'.
Dropping the cache entirely sends every read straight to the database — too costly for the most critical homepage data.

q: 「写完数据库就删缓存」这种朴素失效方式有哪些真实问题？（多选）
q_en: What real problems does naive delete-cache-after-write create? Select all that apply.
scenario: 商品改价后要求 1 秒内全球可见，而这份数据同时缓存在应用层、CDN 和浏览器里。
scenario_en: A price change must be visible worldwide within a second, but the data is cached in the app layer, the CDN, and browsers at the same time.
options: 该删哪些缓存说不清：应用缓存、CDN、浏览器缓存都可能存着旧值
失效请求本身可能失败
删除之后、新值写入之前，另一个请求可能读到旧数据并把它重新缓存回去（竞态条件）
删除操作会锁住整张表
why: 多层缓存、失效失败、删后重缓存竞态——这三个坑让「直接删」在需要立即可见的场景不可靠，于是才有版本化方案。
why_en: Naive delete-on-write fails because caches live in many layers, invalidations can fail, and a racing read can re-cache stale data right after the delete.
options_en: It's unclear which caches to clear — app cache, CDN, and browser cache may all hold stale values.
The invalidation request itself can fail.
Between the delete and the new write, another request can re-cache the stale value — a race condition.
The delete operation locks the entire table.
optionExplanations: 对，应用缓存、CDN、浏览器缓存可能各自都存了一份旧值，光删一处根本不够。
对，失效请求本身可能因为网络或服务故障失败，旧值就这样留下来了。
对，删除和新值写入之间有个窗口，另一个请求正好可能在这个窗口把旧值重新缓存回去。
删除一行缓存数据是极快的键值操作，不会去锁住整张数据库表。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the app cache, CDN, and browser cache may each hold their own stale copy, so deleting just one isn't enough.
Right — the invalidation request itself can fail from a network hiccup or service outage, leaving the stale value in place.
Right — there's a window between the delete and the new write where another request can re-cache the stale value.
Deleting one cache entry is a fast key-value operation; it has no reason to lock an entire database table.

q: 缓存版本化 (cache versioning) 的读写流程是？
q_en: What is the read/write flow for cache versioning?
scenario: 用户资料改动要立即可见，团队放弃删除失效，改用版本号来路由缓存 key。
scenario_en: Profile edits must be visible immediately, so the team drops delete-based invalidation and routes cache keys by version number.
options: 每一次读取都直接绕开缓存去查数据库
写入时主动向所有缓存层都逐个广播一条失效消息通知
版本号存放在缓存里，由缓存自己负责自增
版本号存数据库，随更新递增；读时用版本拼 key
why: 核心是「不删除、改路由」：旧缓存条目从不被删，只是版本一变就没人再读它；CDN 和浏览器缓存也随 key/URL 变化自然过期。
why_en: Each record's version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction, so reads build a versioned cache key and old entries simply become unreachable.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["读请求"] --> V["取版本号
(版本 key 或 DB)"] V --> K["拼 key: event:123:v42"] K --> C{"缓存命中?"} C -->|是| Out["返回"] C -->|否| DB[(数据库)] --> F["回填 v42"] --> Out
options_en: Every single read bypasses the cache and hits the database directly.
On write, actively broadcast an invalidation message to every cache layer one by one.
The version number lives in the cache itself and increments on its own.
The version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction; reads use it to build the cache key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把版本号编进缓存 key，更新后旧 key 自然不可达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Versioned keys embed a version number in the cache key so old keys become unreachable after an update.

optionExplanations: 如果每次读都直接查库，缓存版本化这一整套机制就没有存在的意义了。
广播失效消息到所有缓存层正是版本化想避开的做法，它靠 key 自然不可达而不是主动通知。
版本号若由缓存自己维护，写入数据库的变更就没法可靠触发它递增。
对，版本号存在数据库、跟数据同一事务递增，读时用这个版本号拼出缓存 key。
optionExplanations_en: If every read hit the database directly, the whole point of cache versioning would disappear.
Broadcasting invalidation to every cache layer is exactly what versioning avoids — it relies on keys becoming unreachable, not active notification.
If the cache itself owned the version number, a database write couldn't reliably trigger it to increment.
Right — the version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction as the data, and reads use it to build the cache key.

q: 为什么版本化能整类地绕开失效竞态？
q_en: Why does versioning avoid a whole class of invalidation races?
scenario: 高并发下「删缓存后、写新值前」总有读请求把旧值回填回来，团队评估版本化方案。
scenario_en: Under high concurrency a read keeps refilling the old value between the delete and the new write, so the team evaluates versioning.
options: 因为它给每一次读请求都强行加上了一把全局锁
因为版本递增是原子的，旧缓存被绕开而非删除
因为缓存从这一刻起就再也不会失效了
因为它彻底禁止了任何形式的并发写入
why: 没有删除就没有「删了又被写回旧值」的竞态；版本变化原子发生，读者自动切到新 key，无需广播失效。
why_en: Version changes are atomic in the database so keys never collide and readers move to the new key automatically, eliminating the whole class of invalidation races.
options_en: Because it forcibly adds a single global lock to every read request.
Because version increments are atomic in the database, so old cache entries are bypassed rather than deleted.
Because the cache stops going stale from this point onward, permanently.
Because it forbids any form of concurrent writing whatsoever.
optionExplanations: 全局锁会把所有读串行化，代价太大，而且版本化压根不需要靠锁来避免竞态。
对，版本递增和数据更新在同一事务里原子发生，旧 key 没人再拼出来，自然被绕开而不是被删除。
版本化条目仍然可以设 TTL 自然失效，说"永不失效"不准确。
版本化不禁止并发写，它只是让每次写都产生一个新版本号，写照样能并发发生。
optionExplanations_en: A global lock would serialize every read, far too costly, and versioning doesn't need a lock to avoid races anyway.
Right — the version increment and the data update happen atomically in the same transaction, so nobody constructs the old key anymore and it's simply bypassed, not deleted.
Versioned entries can still carry a TTL and go stale on their own — saying it never lapses isn't accurate.
Versioning doesn't forbid concurrent writes; it just means each write produces a new version number, and writes can still happen concurrently.

q: 缓存版本化的代价包括？
q_en: What costs come with cache versioning?
scenario: 已上线版本化缓存的商品服务，现在还想用它失效「推荐列表」这类计算型结果。
scenario_en: A product service already running versioned caches now wants to use the same trick for computed results like recommendation lists.
options: 多一次查找、旧版本堆积，只适合单实体缓存
读性能会因此直接下降整整十倍
数据库的写入吞吐量会因此直接减半
版本号一旦发生溢出就会直接导致整个系统故障
why: 版本化的三笔账：多一跳查版本、旧条目靠 TTL 清、只覆盖单实体缓存——计算型数据的失效要另想办法（如删除项缓存）。
why_en: Versioning costs an extra lookup per read, lets old versions accumulate until TTLs clean them, and only really fits single-entity caches.
options_en: Every read needs two cache lookups, old versions accumulate, and it only fits single-entity caches.
Read performance ends up dropping by a full factor of ten.
Database write throughput ends up getting cut in half.
A version-number overflow would directly crash the entire system.
optionExplanations: 对，每次读要多查一次版本号，旧版本条目靠 TTL 慢慢清，而且这套机制主要适合单实体缓存。
多出的只是一次额外查找，不至于把读性能拖慢十倍这么夸张。
版本化发生在读路径和 key 构造上，跟数据库的写吞吐没有直接关系。
版本号一般是整数或时间戳，正常场景下不会轻易溢出到让系统故障的地步。
optionExplanations_en: Right — each read needs one extra version lookup, old versions linger until TTL cleans them, and this mainly suits single-entity caches.
The added cost is one extra lookup — nowhere near enough to make reads ten times slower.
Versioning affects the read path and key construction, not the database's write throughput directly.
Version numbers are typically integers or timestamps and don't realistically overflow into a system failure.

scenario: 内容审核场景：帖子被删除后必须立刻从所有已缓存的 feed 中消失，但逐一失效所有包含它的 feed 缓存太贵。
scenario_en: In a content-moderation flow, deleted posts must disappear from all cached feeds immediately, but invalidating every feed containing the post is too expensive.
q: 高效的折中方案是？
q_en: What is the efficient compromise?
options: 清空全部 feed 缓存
把所有 feed 缓存的 TTL 统一降到只有 1 秒
停止缓存所有 feed
维护小的「已删除条目缓存」，出 feed 时过滤
why: 小而快的删除项缓存让你立即遮蔽被删内容、继续服务「大体正确」的缓存数据，复杂结构的真正失效异步完成。
why_en: A small deleted-items cache filters recently removed IDs at serve time so cached feeds stay usable while the expensive invalidation happens in the background.
whenOtherWins: 单实体数据（用户资料、活动详情）用版本化 key 更干净；删除项缓存专攻计算型/聚合缓存的快速遮蔽。
options_en: Wipe the entire feed cache.
Uniformly drop every feed cache's TTL down to just one second.
Stop caching feeds altogether.
Keep a small deleted-items cache of recently removed post IDs and filter them out when serving feeds.
tradeoff: 即时遮蔽 vs 后台彻底失效

termDefinitions.term: 已删除条目缓存 / deleted items cache
termDefinitions.meaning: 一份记录近期被删除或隐藏内容 ID 的小缓存，用于过滤。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deleted-items cache is a small cache of recently removed or hidden IDs used to filter results.

optionExplanations: 清空整个 feed 缓存会让所有用户瞬间全部未命中，代价远大于问题本身。
把 TTL 压到 1 秒等于放弃 feed 缓存的大部分收益，为了一个删除场景牺牲太多。
彻底停止缓存 feed 意味着每次刷新都直接查库，读压力直接反弹到数据库。
对，维护一份小的已删除 ID 缓存，出 feed 时顺手过滤掉，真正的失效可以异步慢慢做。
optionExplanations_en: Wiping the entire feed cache sends every user into a miss at once — a cost far bigger than the problem it solves.
Dropping TTL to one second gives up most of the feed cache's benefit just to handle deletion.
Stopping feed caching entirely means every refresh hits the database directly, bouncing the read load right back.
Right — keep a small cache of recently deleted IDs and filter them out at serve time, while the real invalidation happens asynchronously.

q: 全球 CDN 场景下的缓存失效有什么额外难点与对策？
q_en: What extra challenge does cache invalidation have with a global CDN, and what is the response?
scenario: 内容站在 200 个边缘节点缓存页面，法务要求下架内容 1 分钟内全球不可见。
scenario_en: A content site caches pages at 200 edge nodes, and legal requires taken-down content to be globally invisible within one minute.
options: CDN 的失效指令会瞬间在全球所有节点生效，无需特殊处理
要清数百个边缘节点，传播有延迟；关键更新可跳过 CDN
CDN 这类基础设施完全不支持任何形式的主动失效
只能被动等待所有边缘节点各自的 TTL 慢慢自然过期
why: CDN 失效是「清几百个边缘」而非一个缓存，传播要时间；所以关键数据宁可不进 CDN，次要数据靠边缘短 TTL + 应用层长 TTL 分层。
why_en: Invalidating a CDN means clearing hundreds of edge locations with propagation delay, so critical updates may bypass CDN caching entirely via cache headers.
options_en: A CDN invalidation instantly takes effect at every global node with no special handling needed.
You must clear hundreds of edge nodes with propagation delay; critical updates can bypass the CDN via cache headers.
CDN infrastructure like this doesn't support any form of active invalidation at all.
You can only passively wait for every edge node's own TTL to lapse naturally over time.
optionExplanations: 边缘节点数百个，清理指令传播到每一个都要时间，说瞬间全球生效不准确。
对，要逐一清理数百个边缘节点，传播有延迟；对必须立即可见的关键更新可以绕开 CDN 缓存。
主流 CDN 都提供失效/清除接口，说完全不支持是不准确的。
被动等 TTL 自然过期对紧急更新太慢，主动失效或跳过 CDN 都是可用的对策。
optionExplanations_en: There are hundreds of edge nodes, and propagating a purge to every one takes time — 'instant globally' isn't accurate.
Right — clearing hundreds of edge nodes takes propagation time, so truly critical updates can bypass CDN caching via headers.
Mainstream CDNs all expose invalidation or purge APIs — saying they support none isn't accurate.
Waiting for natural TTL expiry everywhere is too slow for urgent updates; active invalidation or bypassing the CDN are real options.

q: 把「场馆地址更新必须立即可见」的缓存决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the cache decision chain for venue address updates that must be visible immediately in order.
steps: 缓解：给旧版本条目设 TTL 兜底清理，接受每次读多一跳
需求：更新后立刻可见，而数据缓存在 Redis / CDN / 浏览器多层，直接删缓存有竞态
代价：每次读要先取版本号再取数据，旧版本条目会堆积
选型：缓存版本化——版本号入库、同事务递增、key 携带版本
why: 需求（立即可见 + 多层缓存）→ 选型（版本化 key）→ 代价（双查找、旧条目堆积）→ 缓解（TTL 清理）。决策链四段式。
why_en: The chain runs requirement, choice, cost, mitigation: immediate visibility across cache layers leads to versioned keys, whose double lookup and accumulation are bounded by TTL cleanup.

q: 补全 Bitly 缓存策略的推理：
q_en: Complete the reasoning for Bitly's cache strategy.
text: Bitly 是缓存的梦想场景：长短链映射{{不可变}}（创建后从不改变）、读写比{{极端悬殊}}（建一次、读百万次），所以可以激进缓存甚至{{不设过期}}，数据库只接冷门链接的未命中。
why: 「不可变 + 读爆炸」意味着缓存零陈旧风险、命中率极高——这是判断「能多激进地缓存」的标尺。
why_en: Because the mapping is immutable and read millions of times per write, Bitly can cache aggressively with no expiration at all.

scenario: 同一个系统里：用户资料可容忍 5 分钟陈旧，活动场馆地址更新必须立即可见。
scenario_en: In one system, user profiles may be stale for 5 minutes, while event venue address updates must be visible immediately.
q: 正确的整体缓存设计原则是？
q_en: What is the right overall caching design principle?
options: 全站统一 5 分钟 TTL 省事
全站统一都采用最强的那一套失效方案，以防万一
按数据设计：不同数据一致性需求不同，别一刀切
干脆都不缓存
why: 缓存策略应围绕各类数据的一致性需求分层设计；一刀切要么太贵、要么太陈旧。
why_en: Design caching around each data type's consistency needs instead of applying one approach everywhere.
whenOtherWins: 若系统里所有数据的陈旧容忍确实一致，统一策略当然更简单。
options_en: Use one uniform 5-minute TTL everywhere for simplicity.
Apply the single strongest invalidation strategy uniformly everywhere, just in case.
Design per data type: different data has different consistency needs, so don't apply one approach everywhere.
Just don't cache anything.
tradeoff: 统一简单 vs 按需分层保护
optionExplanations: 统一 5 分钟 TTL 会让场馆地址这类要求立即可见的数据也拖上 5 分钟陈旧，违反需求。
全站都上最强失效方案会让用户资料这类能忍陈旧的数据也背上不必要的复杂度和成本。
对，按每类数据自己的一致性需求分层设计——资料可以 TTL，场馆地址要主动失效或跳过缓存。
都不缓存等于放弃用户资料这类能忍陈旧数据的全部缓存收益，代价过大。
optionExplanations_en: A blanket 5-minute TTL would leave venue-address updates, which must be visible immediately, stale for 5 minutes too — violating the requirement.
Applying the strongest invalidation everywhere saddles tolerant data like user profiles with needless complexity and cost.
Right — design per data type's own consistency needs: profiles can use a TTL, venue addresses need active invalidation or no caching at all.
Caching nothing throws away all caching benefit for data like profiles that can easily tolerate staleness — too costly.

q: 缓存和读副本各该用在哪类数据？
q_en: Which data should go to a cache versus a read replica?
scenario: 读密集服务里两类数据：短链→长链映射几乎永不变；账户设置这类数据改动不频繁但改后必须尽快让所有人看到。
scenario_en: In a read-heavy service, short→long URL mappings almost never change, while account settings change rarely but must be visible to everyone soon after a change.
options: 不变的内容激进缓存，需新鲜的数据走读副本
两类都激进缓存，账户设置靠短 TTL 反复失效兜底
两类都只走读副本，不引入缓存层省掉失效管理
按流量高低分：高流量走缓存，低流量走读副本
why: 几乎不变的内容激进缓存换极致读性能，代价是 TTL 内可能陈旧；需保持新鲜的数据靠读副本承接读量，只差一个复制延迟、省掉失效难题。
why_en: Cache content that rarely changes for sub-millisecond reads, and lean on read replicas for data that must stay fresh so you avoid invalidation headaches.
options_en: Cache immutable content aggressively; route freshness-critical data to read replicas.
Cache both aggressively, repeatedly invalidating settings via short TTLs as a backstop.
Send both to read replicas only and add no cache layer, to avoid managing invalidation.
Split by traffic level: high-traffic to cache, low-traffic to read replicas.
tradeoff: 极致读性能+陈旧风险 vs 保持新鲜

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主库复制数据、只承接读请求的副本，数据近实时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica copies data from the primary and serves only reads, staying near-real-time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生存时间：缓存条目的固定有效期，到期即失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is the fixed lifetime of a cache entry, after which it expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库写入传播到副本的时间差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication lag is the delay between a write on the primary and its arrival on a replica.

optionExplanations: 对，选型轴是新鲜度而非流量：永不变的映射激进缓存吃满命中率，改后要尽快可见的数据交给读副本。
账户设置改后要尽快可见，长 TTL 拖慢可见性、短 TTL 又损命中率，反复失效不如直接交给读副本。
永不变的映射交给读副本会白白放弃亚毫秒命中和对主库的零打扰，性价比远不如缓存。
流量高低不是决定轴——决定轴是数据变不变、要不要保持新鲜。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the axis is freshness, not traffic: cache immutable mappings for hit rate, and route freshness-critical data to replicas.
Settings must show up soon after a change; a long TTL delays it and a short one kills hit rate, so a replica beats repeated invalidation.
Serving immutable mappings from a replica throws away sub-millisecond hits and zero primary load — worse value than caching.
Traffic level isn't the deciding axis; whether the data changes and must stay fresh is.

q: 读扩展模式在这里该怎么定位？
q_en: How should read-scaling patterns be positioned here?
scenario: 设计库存管理系统：陈旧的库存数会导致真实超卖，一致性要求高，读写比也就 3:1 左右。
scenario_en: Designing an inventory system: stale stock counts cause real overselling, consistency demands are high, and the read/write ratio is only about 3:1.
options: 读扩展不主攻；要用也配激进失效+更短 TTL
照内容型应用那样激进缓存并设长 TTL 提升命中
彻底禁止缓存和读副本，一切读都直查主库
把堆读副本当作主要扩展手段来分摊读压力
why: 陈旧数据会造成真实损失（超卖）的强一致系统，本就不该主攻读扩展；这些模式仍可用，但要配激进失效和更短 TTL 把陈旧窗口压到最小。
why_en: Strongly consistent systems where stale data causes real harm shouldn't lead with read scaling; you can still use these patterns but with aggressive invalidation and shorter TTLs.
whenOtherWins: 若系统里某些字段其实能容忍陈旧（如商品描述、分类标签），那部分仍可照常激进缓存加长 TTL。
options_en: Read scaling isn't the lead; if used, pair it with aggressive invalidation and shorter TTLs.
Cache aggressively with long TTLs like a content app to push up the hit rate.
Ban caching and read replicas entirely and send every read straight to the primary.
Make piling on read replicas the primary way to spread read load.
tradeoff: 读扩展的陈旧收益 vs 强一致的正确性

termDefinitions.meaning: 读总能拿到最新写入的一致性保证，陈旧不可接受。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency guarantees reads always see the latest write, so staleness is unacceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生存时间：缓存条目的固定有效期，到期即失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is the fixed lifetime of a cache entry, after which it expires.

optionExplanations: 对，超卖类强一致系统把读扩展当『不该主攻』类别；真要缓存就用激进失效+短 TTL 压住陈旧窗口。
长 TTL 会让库存数陈旧到足以超卖，正是这类系统最不能接受的失败。
一刀切禁掉太极端——能容忍陈旧的旁支字段仍可缓存，只是核心库存要强一致。
读写比才 3:1、瓶颈在写一致，堆读副本解决不了超卖，复制延迟还会加剧陈旧。
optionExplanations_en: Right — oversell-prone strongly consistent systems treat read scaling as a 'not the main focus' category; if caching, use aggressive invalidation and short TTLs.
A long TTL lets stock counts go stale enough to oversell — exactly the failure these systems can't accept.
A blanket ban is too extreme — staleness-tolerant fields can still be cached; only the core stock path needs strong consistency.
At a 3:1 ratio the bottleneck is write consistency; replicas don't fix overselling and their lag makes staleness worse.

q: 把 Ticketmaster 的购买路径也放到读副本上会发生什么故障？
q_en: What breaks if Ticketmaster's purchase path also reads from a read replica?
scenario: Ticketmaster 开票瞬间：浏览活动页走读副本没问题，但假设实际购买也从落后 200ms 的读副本读座位余量再下单。
scenario_en: At Ticketmaster's on-sale moment browsing hits read replicas fine, but suppose the actual purchase also reads seat availability from a replica 200ms behind before committing.
options: 两买家都从旧副本读到有票，各自预留同座→超卖
购买延迟升高但结果始终正确，副本最终自行补正
副本自动拒绝购买写请求，用户直接看到下单报错
已售座位在副本上的库存记录被永久覆盖并丢失
why: 座位卖出后主库已更新，但副本还落后 200ms；此窗口内两个买家都从旧副本读到『有票』并各自下单 → 同一座位超卖。修法：浏览走读副本，购买必须查主库权威库存并用锁/事务原子预留；代价是主库承接了购买写压力。
why_en: After a seat sells, the primary is updated but the replica lags 200ms, so two buyers both read 'available' and both reserve the same seat — an oversell; purchases must read the authoritative primary and reserve atomically.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Buyer A
    participant B as Buyer B
    participant P as Primary
    participant R as Lagging Replica
    A->>P: buy seat 12C (reserve)
    P-->>A: OK
    B->>R: read availability
    R-->>B: seat 12C available (stale)
    B->>P: buy seat 12C
    Note over A,B: oversold — purchase must read primary
options_en: Both buyers read 'available' from the stale replica and each reserves the same seat — oversell.
Purchases get slower but stay correct; the replica eventually self-corrects.
The replica auto-rejects the purchase write, so the user sees an immediate order error.
The sold seat's stock record on the replica gets permanently overwritten and lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主库复制数据、只承接读请求的副本，可能落后于主库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica copies data from the primary and serves reads, possibly lagging behind.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库写入传播到副本的时间差，此处约 200ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication lag is the delay before a primary's write reaches a replica, here about 200ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一库存/座位被卖给多个买家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overselling is selling the same inventory or seat to more than one buyer.

optionExplanations: 对，复制延迟窗口内副本仍显示『有票』，两买家各自读到旧值并下单，同座被卖两次。
问题不是延迟，而是从落后副本读到的库存本身就是错的，副本不会补正这次超卖。
副本本就不接写请求；这里的错误是从它读到了陈旧库存，不是它拒绝写。
副本落后不代表数据丢失——已售数据安全在主库，只是还没传播到副本。
optionExplanations_en: Right — within the lag window the replica still shows 'available', so both buyers read the stale value and commit, selling the seat twice.
The issue isn't latency; the stock read from the lagging replica is simply wrong, and the replica won't undo this oversell.
A replica never takes writes anyway; the bug is reading stale stock from it, not it rejecting writes.
A lagging replica doesn't lose data — sold data is safe on the primary, just not yet propagated.

q: 物化视图的平均分何时才会反映新评论？
q_en: When does a materialized view's average reflect a new review?
scenario: 商品平均评分用物化视图预计算，由后台作业每 10 分钟重算一次；用户刚提交一条新评论。
scenario_en: Product average ratings are precomputed in a materialized view rebuilt by a background job every 10 minutes; a user just submitted a new review.
options: 要等下次后台重算才更新，刷新周期即陈旧上限
新评论一写入就被物化视图实时增量重算并反映
每次页面加载都会触发一次全表聚合重算
物化视图永不自动更新，必须人工手动重建
why: 物化视图是落地存储的预计算结果，不随底表实时变；它靠后台作业周期重算，两次重算之间读到的都是旧聚合，所以刷新周期就是陈旧上限。要更新，就得刷得更勤——代价是每次全表聚合的计算开销。
why_en: A materialized view stores precomputed results that don't update with the base tables; a background job recomputes it periodically, so the refresh interval is the staleness ceiling.
options_en: It waits for the next background rebuild; the refresh interval is the staleness ceiling.
The new review is incrementally recomputed into the materialized view in real time.
Every page load triggers a full-table aggregation recompute.
The materialized view never auto-updates and must be rebuilt manually.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 join+聚合的结果落地存储，读时零计算，靠后台作业周期刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A materialized view stores the result of a join/aggregation on disk for zero-compute reads, refreshed by a periodic background job.

optionExplanations: 对，聚合值只在后台作业重算时刷新，两次重算之间读到旧值，所以刷新周期决定最大陈旧。
物化视图存的是上次算好的值，底表插入一条评论不会触发它自动增量重算。
预计算的意义正是避免每次加载现算；每次都重算就退化回了昂贵的实时聚合。
它不是永不更新——由后台作业按周期自动重算，只是不是实时的。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the aggregate refreshes only when the background job reruns, so reads between runs are stale and the interval sets the max staleness.
A materialized view holds the last computed value; inserting one review into the base table won't trigger an incremental recompute.
Precomputing exists precisely to avoid recomputing on every load; doing so reverts to the expensive live aggregation.
It isn't never-updating — a background job rebuilds it on a schedule, just not in real time.
